Online:Combat:
{{Trail|Hints}}[[Category:Online-Combat]]
'''Combat''' in [[Online:Online|Elder Scrolls Online]] is dynamic. The game offers players a variety of visual and auditory cues about which actions may be appropriate next, including marking the area of impending enemy attacks in red, or by prompting the user to block or interrupt.

==Basic Combat Actions==
All players have a variety of abilities that they can use in combat, which do not require any skills to be learned or slotted. Some of these have associated passive skills which reduce their cost or improve their effectiveness.

===[[ON:Light Attack|Light Attack]]===
This is a quick attack that can be performed with any weapon. If an opponent is targeted and in range, it will damage the opponent. It is performed by tapping the attack button.

Light attacks require no {{ESO Stamina Link}} or {{ESO Magicka Link}}. The damage of light attacks, regardless of weapon type, scales with your highest offensive stats. [https://forums.elderscrollsonline.com/en/discussion/550927/pc-mac-patch-notes-v6-2-5-markarth-update-28#latest Prior to Update 28], the damage of light attacks scaled with your {{ESO Stamina Link|Maximum}} and {{ESO Weapon Damage Link}}, or {{ESO Magicka Link|Maximum}} and {{ESO Spell Damage Link}} for staves.

Hitting a light attack while in combat gives you a hidden buff which generates {{ESO Ultimate Link|3}} every second for 9 seconds and resets its duration every time you hit a light attack while in combat.

===[[ON:Heavy Attack|Heavy Attack]]===
This is an attack which must be charged. It does more damage per attack than light attacks, though less damage per second due to the charging time. There may also be further effects. Using a heavy attack against an [[ON:Off Balance|Off Balance]] opponent will knock them down, deal 70% more damage and restore double the resources. Heavy attacks are performed by holding the attack button.

Heavy attacks require no {{ESO Stamina Link}} or {{ESO Magicka Link}}. The damage of heavy attack, regardless of weapon type, scales with your highest offensive stats. [https://forums.elderscrollsonline.com/en/discussion/550927/pc-mac-patch-notes-v6-2-5-markarth-update-28#latest Prior to Update 28], the damage of heavy attacks scaled with your {{ESO Stamina Link|Maximum}} and {{ESO Weapon Damage Link}}, or {{ESO Magicka Link|Maximum}} and {{ESO Spell Damage Link}} for staves. The return of either stamina or magicka resource points from a heavy attack is still determined by weapon type: staves restore magicka, while bows and melee weapons give you a return in stamina.

* Releasing the attack button before it is fully charged will still result in an attack, which deals more damage than a light attack, but will not restore resources or trigger certain sets or abilities which call for a "fully charged" heavy attack.  This is sometimes referred to as a "medium attack" in patch notes.

* Heavy attacks restore {{ESO Magicka Link}} (with staves) or {{ESO Stamina Link}} (other weapons) when fully charged. The amount restored scales to the length of time that the heavy attack takes to charge, so for example, a heavy attack with a 2-handed weapon will restore more {{ESO Stamina Link}} than when dual wielding. The amount restored also scales with player level.

* Restoration staves and Lightning staves will begin channeling damage as soon as the heavy attack begins. This can be a detriment if you don't want to catch the attention of an enemy until the attack is fully charged.

* Heavy attacks with a Frost Staff used to [[ON:Taunt|Taunt]] an enemy if you had points in the [[ON:Tri Focus|Tri Focus]] skill. As of [https://forums.elderscrollsonline.com/en/discussion/550927/pc-mac-patch-notes-v6-2-5-markarth-update-28#latest Update 28], this taunt was moved to [[ON:Destructive Touch|Destructive Clench]].

===[[ON:Block|Block]]ing===
[[File:ON-misc-Block.jpg|thumb|right|A Tank charging a Power Bash. Note the yellow lines that indicate this attack should be blocked.]]
Blocking can be performed with any weapon and even when unarmed. For most attacks, a successful block will reduce your damage taken and prevent any negative disabling effects associated with that attack. The cost of blocking depends on the player's level. Blocking an enemy's heavy attack will set it [[ON:Off Balance|Off Balance]]. It is not possible to light attack or heavy attack while blocking.  

* Damage from areas dealing damage over time (DoT) like [[ON:Wall of Elements|Wall of Elements]] and effects that are on or inside characters such as [[ON:Daedric Curse|Daedric Curse]] cannot be blocked.

* Secondary effects associated with attacks (such as the Major Breach from [[ON:Disintegrating Dragonsbreath|Disintegrating Dragonsbreath]]) cannot be blocked, even if the main damage from the attack can.

* Pressing the attack key while blocking does a Bash. Bash is a melee range attack with your weapon dealing physical damage to the enemy. It interrupts enemies and can trigger your weapon's poisons and enchantments. If you interrupt an enemy with a bash, the bash's damage is increased.
{{NewLine}}

===[[ON:Roll Dodge|Roll Dodging]]===
[[File:ON-misc-dodgeroll.jpg|thumb|right|A Fire Mage and his Fire Rune. Note the red circle that indicates this area should be avoided.]]
[[Online:Area of Effect|Area of Effect]] attacks are often indicated as red areas. Roll dodging allows the player to roll in a given direction in order to escape an area of effect or break free of a rooting effect. The {{ESO Stamina Link}} cost of dodging depends on the player's level. When rolling, all incoming attacks will automatically miss. Roll dodging also disables collision with all NPCs, so you can roll right through any enemy.  This is useful for escaping if you're surrounded, but can also be used outside of combat to get past NPCs who are in your way. Performing a roll dodge will give the player dodge roll fatigue, increasing the cost of consecutive rolls until the effect dissipates.

* Damage from ground target AOEs like [[ON:Wall of Elements|Wall of Elements]] or [[ON:Caltrops|Caltrops]] and effects that are on or inside characters such as [[ON:Daedric Curse|Daedric Curse]] cannot be dodged.

* Damage from magical AOEs such as [[ON:Drain Power|Drain Power]] and beams such as [[ON:Soul Assault|Soul Assault]] or the heavy attacks from restoration and lightning staves cannot be dodged. The last AoE tick from a lightning staff heavy attack is the exception to this and can be dodged.

{{NewLine}}

===[[ON:Interrupt|Interrupt]]ing===
[[File:ON-misc-interrupt.jpg|thumb|right|A Fire Mage charging Heat Wave. Note the red lines that indicate this attack should be interrupted.]]
Players can interrupt an opponent who is winding up an attack, as long as they are within melee range. Successfully interrupting an opponent stuns them and throws them off balance. The {{ESO Stamina Link}} cost of interrupting depends on the player's level.

* Some active abilities, such as [[Online:Venom Arrow|Venom Arrow]], can also interrupt. There is no additional {{ESO Stamina Link}} cost beyond the normal cost of using the ability.

{{NewLine}}

===[[ON:Break Free|Breaking Free]]===
[[File:ON-misc-breakfree.jpg|thumb|right|A character performing Break Free. Note the swirls at the character's feet that indicate immunity to crowd control.]]
Players can break free of some forms of crowd controlling effects, such as stuns. The {{ESO Stamina Link}} cost of breaking free depends on the player's level. After breaking free, the player gains "{{ESO Icon Abbr|misc|Crowd Control Immunity}} Crowd Control Immunity", which makes them immune to crowd control effects for 7 seconds.

{{NewLine}}

===[[ON:Stealth|Stealth]]===
Stealth enables you to sneak without drawing an enemy's attention, and greatly reduces the distance you can be seen by enemy players in Cyrodiil. Any attack inflicted while you are sneaking and undetected will automatically crit, and you will subsequently stop sneaking. When you are in sneak mode, your {{ESO Stamina Link}} will drain while moving, and recharge when you stand still. Moving in stealth also comes with a significant speed penalty, which can be avoided by using certain sets, or with the [[ON:Vampirism|vampirism]] passive [[ON:Dark Stalker|Dark Stalker]]. You cannot get in stealth and even crouch as a [[ON:Werewolf|Werewolf]]

==Skills==
Players can slot 5 active or toggled [[Online:Skills|abilities]], in addition to a single ultimate ability. These are the main skills that a player uses in combat, and are known as the combat bar.

* Once a player reaches level 15, they can switch between two combat bars. This requires having two different sets of weapons (or weapons and shields).
** You cannot use the same weapon for both bars, but you can use a second identical weapon for the second bar, if you wish.
** The damage and effect of abilities are calculated regarding the bar that was active when the ability is used, even if the effect or damage carry on after bar switching. 

===Active Abilities===
Active abilities usually have an attribute resource cost associated with them.

* Most class abilities require [[Online:Magicka|magicka]]. Some can later be morphed to use [[Online:Stamina|stamina]].
* Most weapon abilities require [[Online:Stamina|stamina]].
** The exception is staff abilities (both [[Online:Destruction_Staff|destruction]] and [[Online:Restoration_Staff|restoration]]), which require magicka.
* Abilities from other skill lines, such as those from factions or armor, usually also require stamina or magicka.

Some active abilities require a hostile target before they can be used. Other abilities may automatically pick a target. Abilities with an area of effect may require the player to target an area on the ground after clicking the key for the ability, while others are simply centered around the player and require no aiming.

===Toggled Abilities===
Some abilities are toggled, which means they remain active until the user disables them. These abilities may have a one-time cost associated with them, in addition to a constant negative effect, such as a resource cost.

* Toggled skills stay active after switching your combat bar, even if the other combat car doesn't have the toggled skill slotted in.

===Ultimate Abilities===
Only one ultimate ability may be slotted at one time. Ultimate abilities charge over time by accumulating points of Ultimate. Damaging an enemy with a light or heavy attack will grant 3 Ultimate per second for 9 seconds. Other effects may also grant additional Ultimate, such as the Major or Minor Heroism effect as well as the Banish the Wicked or Combat Frenzy passives. The weapon [[Online:Traits|trait]] Decisive provides you with a percentage-based chance (up to a maximum of 40%) to gain 1 additional point of Ultimate any time you gain Ultimate normally. Once the ability is fully charged, it may be used.

* Using an ultimate ability completely drains your ultimate points to zero, regardless of whether you had extra ultimate charged.
* Healing a player who is gaining Ultimate will also grant you Ultimate at the same rate.
* You can store up to 500 Ultimate points.

===Slotted Abilities===
While all slotted abilities will fall into one of the above categories, some abilities will also provide a bonus to players simply by being slotted. An example of this is [[Online:Restoring Aura|Restoring Aura]].

===Synergies===
Some skills have [[Online:Synergy|synergies]], which allow allies to perform a variety of beneficial actions once a skill is used. Allies will see a message informing them that they are able to activate the synergy, which has no cost to the player who activates it. Synergies themselves cannot be slotted. Some examples of skills with synergies are [[Online:Lightning Splash|Lightning Splash]] (with the Conduit synergy) or [[Online:Nova|Nova]] (with the Supernova synergy). Each synergy has a cooldown preventing the same player from activating it continuously. Other synergies such as the "Brace for Impact" buff (while fighting [[Online:Lord Warden Dusk|Lord Warden Dusk]] in the [[Online:Imperial City Prison|Imperial City Prison]]) or the "Use Free Ally" synergy (when fighting [[Online:Ruzozuzalpamaz|Ruzozuzalpamaz]] in the [[Online:Crypt of Hearts II|Crypt of Hearts]]) are not related to player skills, but are needed to overcome the mechanics of the boss fight itself. These tend not to have cooldowns and can be activated by anyone.

==Vulnerable States==
Players and opponents can be put into a variety of vulnerable states.  These states can prevent or hinder movement or the ability to attack.  Some abilities, such as [[Online:Ruffian|Ruffian]], affect opponents affected by a subset of effects.

===Disabling Effects===
A disabling effect is one that prevents a character or opponent from attacking.  Players can break out of this state by using Break Free.

====[[ON:Stun|Stun]]====
A stunned character will be slumped over while kneeling.  An example of a skill that stuns is [[Online:Summon Storm Atronach|Summon Storm Atronach]].

====[[ON:Off Balance|Off Balance]]====
[[File:ON-misc-Offbalance.jpg|thumb|right|A Fire Mage that was set off-balance. Note the white swirls.]]
An off balance character will stand dizzily for a short time, being stunned and made vulnerable to some skills such as [[ON:Flame Lash|Flame Lash]].  Opponents whose heavy attacks are blocked will become off-balance, as will some opponents performing specific attacks (such as a [[ON:Kagouti|Kagouti]] charging).  Using a heavy attack on an off-balance opponent will knock them down, deal 70% more damage and restore 70% more resources. Note that enemies with Crowd Control Immunity can still be put Off Balance but will not be stunned. An example of an ability that can set opponents off-balance is [[Online:Lava Whip|Lava Whip]].

{{NewLine}}

====[[ON:Fear|Fear]]====
[[File:ON-misc-Feared.jpg|thumb|right|A character feared by a Dremora Fearkyn]]
A character who is feared runs away in a random direction or cowers in place.  Fear is cast by some unique monsters as well as some player abilities, including [[Online:Aspect of Terror|Aspect of Terror]] and the [[Online:Werewolf Transformation|Werewolf Transformation]] ultimate.

{{NewLine}}

====[[ON:Silence|Silence]]====
[[File:ON-misc-Silence.jpg|thumb|right|An NPC casting Negate Magic (the purple bubble)]]
Silenced characters are unable to use {{ESO Magicka Link}}-based abilities, but are still able to move freely and use {{ESO Stamina Link}}-based abilities and Light and Heavy Attacks. Despite its in-game definition, this effect also impedes the use of abilities with {{ESO Health Link}} or {{ESO Ultimate Link}} costs, as well as abilities with no resource cost.

The only instance of this effect available to player characters is [[Online:Negate Magic|Negate Magic]], but it also exists in skills only available to enemies, such as a [[ON:Dro-m'Athra Sun-Eater|Dro-m'Athra Sun-Eater's]] Eclipse Field.

{{NewLine}}

===Partially Disabling Effects===
Some effects are less severe than full disabling effects, and still allow characters to attack in some form. Breaking free does not remove these effects. Most of the flying enemies have "Flying Immunities" which makes them immune to snares and roots.

====[[ON:Immobilize|Root]]====
Rooted or Immobilized characters cannot walk or run, but they are still able to attack, block and cast spells. An ability that roots is [[Online:Dark Talons|Dark Talons]].

* Players can escape a rooting effect by dodge rolling.
* Dashes such as [[Online:Bolt Escape|Bolt Escape]] allows a player to move, but the rooting effect will still be active on them. Similarly, NPC shock mages will be able to teleport while rooted.

====[[ON:Movement Speed|Snare]]====
Snare effects reduce a character's movement speed, but do not otherwise hinder the character's ability to use attacks or other abilities.  Snaring appears as a gray cloud at the character's feet. This very common effect can be triggered by abilities such as [[Online:Caltrops|Caltrops]].

* The only way to remove a snare is to dispel the effect with an ability such as [[Online:Purge|Purge]] or [[Online:Expunge|Expunge]].
* All enemies can apply a ~60% snare called "Hamstrung" for 5 seconds if they hit you while you move away from them with your back on their side.

===Status Effects===
Upon damaging with certain types of damage there is a chance to cause certain debilitating effects to an enemy which either deal damage over time or apply a debuff to an enemy. These effects are called status effects.

Chances of applying status effect are different for different types of attacks and are as follows:
{|class=wikitable
!Attack type!!|Chance to apply status effect
|-
|Weapon Enchantment's damage||20% base chance
|-
|Weapon Alchemical Poison's damage||20% base chance
|-
|Single-target direct attack ability||10% base chance
|-
|Area-of-effect abilities||5 % base chance
|-
|Single-target damage-over-time abilities||3% base chance
|-
|Area-of-effect damage-over-time abilities||1% base chance
|-
|All weapons' Light and Heavy attack||0% base chance
|-
|[[ON:Werewolf|Werewolf]] Light/Partially Charged/Heavy attack|| 3%/5%/10% base chance
|}
Damage-over-time abilities have a chance to apply status effect on every tick of damage.

The base chance of applying status effect can be multiplied by the [[ON:Charged|Charged]] weapon trait, Skill Passives like [[ON:Elemental_Force|Elemental Force]] from the [[ON:Destruction_Staff|Destruction staff]] [[ON:Skills|skill]] tree, Sets like [[ON:Threads of War|Threads of War]] and the [[ON:Champion|Champion]] passives [[ON:Champion#Extended Might|Flawless Ritual]] and [[ON:Champion#Extended Might|Battle Mastery]].
====[[ON:Burning|Burning]]====
The Burning status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Flame Damage|Flame Damage]] to a target. When you apply the Burning status effect on an enemy, they take flame damage over time based on your {{ESO Magicka Link|Max}} and {{ESO Spell Damage Link}}. Burning effect lasts 4 seconds and ticks every 2 seconds.

====[[ON:Chilled|Chilled]]====
The Chilled status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Frost Damage|Frost Damage]] to a target. A Chilled enemy takes instant frost damage and suffers from [[ON:Buffs#Debuffs|Minor Maim]] debuff for 4 seconds, reducing their damage by 5%. If you have an ice staff as your active weapon at the time it is applied, it will also apply [[ON:Buffs#Debuffs|Minor Brittle]], increasing their critical damage taken.

====[[ON:Concussion|Concussion]]====
The Concussion status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Shock Damage|Shock Damage]] to a target. A Concussed enemy takes instant shock damage, increased by 15% if Concussion was already recently applied, and suffers from [[ON:Buffs#Vulnerability|Minor Vulnerability]] for 4 seconds, increasing their damage taken by 5%.

====[[ON:Poisoned|Poisoned]]====
The Poisoned status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Poison Damage|Poison Damage]] to a target. When you apply poisoned status effect on an enemy, they take Poison damage over time, increased by up to 100% based on their missing {{ESO Health Link}}. Poisoned effect lasts 4 seconds and ticks every 2 seconds.

====[[ON:Diseased|Diseased]]====
The Diseased status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Disease Damage|Disease Damage]] to a target. A Diseased enemy takes instant direct disease damage that splashes in a 6 meter radius to enemies, up to once every 4 seconds. The enemy also suffers from [[ON:Buffs#Debuffs|Minor Defile]] debuff for 4 seconds, decreasing their healing received and damage shield strength by 6%.

====[[ON:Hemorrhaging|Hemorrhaging]]====
The Hemorrhaging status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Bleed Damage|Bleed Damage]] to a target. When you apply Hemorrhaging status effect on an enemy, they take bleed damage over time, stacking up to 3 times. Each stack increases the damage by 25%. Hemorrhaging effect lasts 4 seconds and ticks every 2 seconds.

====[[ON:Sundered|Sundered]]====
The Sundered status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Physical Damage|Physical Damage]] to a target. A Sundered enemy takes instant physical damage and suffers from [[ON:Buffs#Debuffs|Minor Breach]] debuff for 4 seconds, decreasing their physical and spell resistance by 2974. Applying Sundered will also increase your {{ESO Weapon Damage Link}} and {{ESO Spell Damage Link}} by 100 for 4 seconds.

====[[ON:Overcharged|Overcharged]]====
The Overcharged status can be applied by dealing [[ON:Magic Damage|Magic Damage]] to a target. An Overcharged enemy takes instant magic damage and restores 65 {{ESO Magicka Link}} to the caster. They also suffer from [[ON:Buffs#Debuffs|Minor Magickasteal]] for 4 seconds, which restores 168 magicka per second to players dealing damage to them.

===Other Effects===
These are common negative effects enemies can apply to players or enemies in Trials and Dungeons. These cannot be removed with skills that say "remove negative effects"

====Hindered====
Healing your missing health is prevented for 12 seconds or until 39,760 points of healing are received. Applied when players blocking specific attacks.

====Rattled==== 
You are shaken up for 12 seconds, reduces your damage done by 70% and increasing your damage taken by 40%. Applied when blocking specific attacks.

====Devitalized====
You are weakened for 8 seconds, Reduces your Physical Resistance and Spell Resistance by 60%, reduces damage shields by 30% and increases damage taken by 30%. Applied when not blocking specific attacks.

====Seethe====
Increases the damage done of the enemy for a moment {{huh|how much and for how long ?}}, as seen by the red glow on the enemy. Applied to the enemy when specific attacks are dodged.

==Unarmed Combat==
Although disadvantageous, it is possible to fight without a [[ON:Weapons|weapon]] equipped. Unarmed damage scales with your level, but you won't have the base damage stats gained by equipping a weapon. A [[ON:Shields|shield]] can be equipped by itself, although it cannot be used while unarmed. Many non-hostile NPCs will use unarmed combat if they see you commit a [[ON:Justice|crime]].

==[[ON:Death|Death]]==
[[File:ON-misc-Death Screen.jpg|thumb|right|Death recap]]
When you die, you are put into a blue-tinted third-person deathcam which can be rotated to look around. You can view a "Death Recap", which displays the last five attacks dealt to you, and three hints relating to the cause of death. Additionally, all equipped items lose durability each time you die to PvE, but item's efficiency won't decrease until you hit 0 durability at which point the item won't provide any benefit. Death to the players in PvP will not decrease equipped items durability. Durability can be restored by using a [[Online:Repair Kits|repair kit]], purchasable from [[Online:Merchants|merchants]]. Most [[ON:Vendors|vendors]] also offer repair services directly, which are usually cheaper and quicker. After dying in PvE, you can resurrect yourself on the spot at the cost of a filled [[Online:Soul Gems|Soul Gem]] or choose to respawn at the nearest [[Online:Wayshrines|wayshrine]]. Group Dungeon/Trial boss fights will prevent respawning until every member of your [[ON:Grouping|group]] is dead (including any quest-related NPC companions in some cases). If you die in PvP, you may respawn at any [[Online:Alliance|Alliance]]-controlled keep that is not under attack and has at least one Alliance-controlled resource, or at a [[Online:Forward Camps|forward camp]] if you are within its radius. Allies may resurrect you on the spot as well, which can prove invaluable in situations where respawning is not an option. However, you cannot remain on the deathcam screen indefinitely and will eventually be forced to respawn at a wayshrine.

==Combat Text==
With Combat Text enabled, floating text will display incoming and outgoing damage and crowd control. Each category of combat text can be found in the Settings menu, under the Interface category.

Online:Death:
{{Trail|Combat}}__NOTOC__[[File:ON-misc-Death Screen.jpg|thumb|right|Death recap]]
'''Death''' occurs when your {{ESO Health Link}} is reduced to zero.  Normally, you will be given the option to revive in place at the cost of a Soul Gem, or respawning at the nearest [[ON:Wayshrines|Wayshrine]].  If you are in an interior area such as a [[ON:Delves|Delve]] or [[ON:Dungeons|Dungeon]], you will respawn at the entrance instead.  If you choose to spend a Soul Gem and revive in place, you will be revived in ghost-form, unable to attack or be damaged for several seconds.  The [[ON:Soul Summons|Soul Summons]] passive in [[ON:Soul Magic|Soul Magic]] can save you a Soul Gem provided you haven't died recently.  If there are allies nearby, they may spend a Soul Gem to [[ON:Resurrect|Resurrect]] you in place without the ghost-phase.  This can be very helpful in boss battles, because if your whole group dies, you'll have to start the battle over.  Each time you die your armor is damaged.

==Death in PvP==
===Cyrodiil===
When you die in [[ON:Cyrodiil|Cyrodiil]] by PvP, you will not have the option to revive in place, but instead be forced to respawn at a [[ON:Keeps|Keep]] of your choice which your [[ON:Alliances|Alliance]] controls, or possibly a [[ON:Forward Camps|Forward Camp]] if one exists.  You may not respawn at a Keep which is currently under attack.  You can still be Resurrected by your allies if any are around.

===Imperial City===
Dying in the Imperial City to most PvE enemies will give you the option to respawn in your current location at the cost of a Soul Gem (giving you several seconds in ghost-form as usual), or to Release, which will cause you to respawn at your Alliance's Rally Point in the District you are in or your section of the [[ON:Imperial Sewers|Imperial Sewers]].  In the case of deaths to PvP enemies, or NPC soldiers of the opposing alliances, the Release option is the only one available.  You will lose [[ON:Tel Var Stones|Tel Var Stones]] in either case, and in the event of a PvP death, the player who killed you will claim those stones.

===Dueling===
Dying in a duel in PvE zones allows you to revive in place for free, without the damage to your armor or spending a Soul Gem, though you still have to spend several seconds in ghost-form.

==Death Recap==
When you die, you have the option to see a recap showing you the most recent source(s) of damage, and possibly providing tips to avoid dying in the same way again. Online:Area of Effect:
{{Trail|Combat}}
'''Area of Effect''' skills ('''AoE''' for short) are attacks which can hit multiple targets within a region.  These can be both hostile attacks and healing or buffs for your allies.  There are 4 general shapes for an area of effect:

* '''Circular''' - affects all targets within a certain radius of the caster
* '''Target Area''' - affects all targets within a chosen circle at a distance from the caster
* '''Conical''' - affects all targets within a conical area in front of the caster
* '''Path''' - affects all targets in a rectangular area in front of the caster

Some skills may change from one type of area to another based on morphs.  Some AOE skills are instantaneous, while others have longer duration.  A list of skills with AOE is below.  (Note that this does not include [[ON:Multiple Target|Multiple Target]] skills, which are different in that they must be used on a single target and may affect other nearby targets as well.  AOE skills can be cast without a specific target.)

==Hostile==
===Circular===
;[[ON:Dragonknight|Dragonknight]]
* [[ON:Ardent Flame|Ardent Flame]] — [[ON:Dragonknight Standard|Dragonknight Standard]]
* [[ON:Draconic Power|Draconic Power]] — [[ON:Dark Talons|Dark Talons]], [[ON:Inhale|Inhale]]
* [[ON:Earthen Heart|Earthen Heart]] — [[ON:Magma Armor|Magma Armor]]

Online:Critical Resistance:
{{Trail|Combat}}
'''Critical Resistance''' reduces the amount of damage you take from Critical Damage.  

==Formula== 
'''Percentage Reduction = (Critical Resistance / [player level, capped at 66])'''

The Percentage Reduction is subtracted from the attacker's Critical Damage bonuses.  

For Example:
Without any bonuses to Critical Damage, an attacker would have a 1.5 Critical Damage bonus. If you have a full set of Impenetrable body armor in gold quality, for 258 * 7 = 1806 Critical Resistance, on a CP160+ character this comes out to 1806 / 66 = 27.4% Percentage Reduction.  This comes out to (1.5 - 0.274) = 1.226 Critical Damage multiplier for incoming damage. In other words, a 1000 damage hit that would normally do 1500 upon critical strike will now only do 1226 damage upon critical strike to the Resistant target (a 22.3% reduction in incoming damage from that Critical Strike).

Critical damage resistance 66 = 1% Critical Damage Reduction.

==Notes==
* A critical strike can never deal less damage than a non-critical strike. If your Critical Resistance would cause the damage to go below that of a non-critical strike, then the damage is limited to the same amount as a non-critical strike.

Online:Animation Canceling:
{{Trail|Combat|addcat1=Hints}}
'''Animation Canceling''' is the practice of using one animation to cancel another, typically to increase damage output.

==Light Attack Weaving==
===Skills===
[[File:ON-misc-Animation Canceling Light Attack Skill.webm|thumb|right|512px|A video showing varying degrees of cancellation of light attacks. When the animation appears to 'jump', the animation has been completely canceled. When the light attack accelerates and finishes faster than it otherwise would have, it has been partially canceled.]]
The most common kind of animation canceling is in Light Attack Weaving, which is when the animation of a light attack is canceled by a skill's animation. This is beneficial for resource generation, increasing the rate at which Ultimate is gained and, depending on situation, other resources. It can also dramatically increase damage output by doubling the amount of triggers for procs and adding the damage of weapons to DPS. It is done by light attacking, and then canceling the animation by using a skill. This can be difficult to master consistently, but a variety of addons are available to help PC players learn to weave. 

Other types of animation canceling are possible, including:
*Canceling heavy attacks with skills
*Canceling skills by swapping bars
*Canceling skills by blocking
Online:Critical Damage:
{{Trail|Combat}}
'''Critical Damage''' is a value that represents the increased damage a given attack will do when performing a Critical Strike. How often you will deal Critical Damage depends upon the higher of your [[ON:Spell Critical (effect)|Spell Critical]] and [[ON: Weapon Critical (effect)|Weapon Critical]]. Critical Damage starts with a base damage increase of 50%, and is capped at 125%. NPCs do not have any [[ON:Critical Resistance|Critical Resistance]], though enemy players will.

There are several ways to increase this:
*[[ON:Races|Racial]] and [[On:Classes|Class]] passives, such as [[ON:Feline Ambush|Feline Ambush]] and [[ON:Aedric Spear|Aedric Spear]].
*[[ON:The Shadow (Mundus Stone)|The Shadow]] Mundus Stone.
*[[ON:Champion Points|Champion Point]] Slottables, [[ON:Fighting Finesse|Fighting Finesse]] and [[ON:Backstabber|Backstabber]].
*[[ON:Major Brittle|Major]] and [[ON:Minor Brittle|Minor]] Brittle.
*[[ON:Major Force|Major]] and [[ON:Minor Force|Minor]] Force.
*Wearing [[ON:Dexterity|Medium armor]] pieces.
*Additionally some sets contain Critical Damage as part of the 5 piece bonus. See : [[:Category:Online-Sets with Increase Critical Damage]]
The mythic item [[ON:Malacath's Band of Brutality|Malacath's Band of Brutality]] '''decreases''' Critical Damage by 50%.

Online:Critical Healing:
{{Trail|Combat}}
'''Critical Healing''' is a value that represents the increased [[ON:Healing|Healing]] a given Ability will do when performing a Critical Strike. How often you will deal Critical Healing depends upon the higher of your [[ON:Spell Critical (effect)|Spell Critical]] and [[ON: Weapon Critical (effect)|Weapon Critical]]. Critical Healing starts with a base Healing increase of 50%, and is capped at 125%.

There are several ways to increase this:
*[[ON:Races|Racial]] and [[On:Classes|Class]] passives, such as [[ON:Feline Ambush|Feline Ambush]].
*[[ON:The Shadow (Mundus Stone)|The Shadow]] Mundus Stone.
*[[ON:Champion Points|Champion Point]] Slottables, [[ON:Fighting Finesse|Fighting Finesse]].
*The [[ON:Energized Salve|Energized Salve]] verse
*Additionally some sets contain Critical Healing as part of the 5 piece bonus. See [[:Category:Online-Sets with Increase Critical Healing]]
Online:Diseased:
{{Trail|Combat}}
{{ESO Icon Abbr|misc|Nature's Grasp}} '''Diseased''' is a debilitating [[Online:Combat#Status Effects|effect]] that can be applied by doing [[ON:Disease Damage|disease damage]]. It deals a single hit of disease damage to the enemy and every 4 seconds it can also burst in a 6 meter area around the enemy, dealing disease damage to all enemies, including the original target. It also applies [[ON:Minor Defile|Minor Defile]] to all targets hit, reducing their [[ON:Healing|Healing]] received and [[ON:Damage Shield|Shields]] strength by 6% This status effect can be removed with a [[ON:Cleansing|Cleansing]] effect.

Online:Crafting:
{{Trail}}[[Category:Online-Crafting]] In ''[[Online:Online|Elder Scrolls Online]]'', there are seven '''crafting''' professions. Skill points are needed to fully develop crafting skills, but you are not limited to a single profession, and can choose to dabble in all of them, or specialize in a few professions. To craft, a [[#Crafting Stations|crafting station]] of appropriate kind must be found. [[Online:Crafting Certification|Crafting Certification]] quests can be completed, which enables access to repeatable [[Online:Crafting Writs|Crafting Writs]] quests. Crafting materials can be gathered from the world, such as plants or ore, or looted from enemies. The primary use is to create items, however several crafting skills allow extracting of materials from items or researching traits they possess, which destroys those items. Some even let you improve existing items. ==Professions== {{TOCright}} *[[Online:Alchemy|Alchemy]]: The practice of binding of two or more [[Online:Reagents|Reagents]] with a [[Online:Alchemy Ingredients#Potion Solvents|Solvent]] to make potions and poisons. *[[Online:Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]]: The art of converting [[Online:Blacksmithing Materials|raw materials]] into and improving upon [[Online:Heavy Armor|heavy armor]] and [[Online:Weapons|metallic weapons]]. *[[Online:Clothing|Clothing]]: The art of converting [[Online:Clothing Materials|raw materials]] into and improving upon [[Online:Light Armor|light]] and [[Online:Medium Armor|medium armor]]. *[[Online:Enchanting|Enchanting]]: The practice of binding [[Online:Runestones|Runes]] into [[Online:Glyphs|Glyphs]] used to enhance weapons, armor, and jewelry. *[[Online:Jewelry Crafting|Jewelry Crafting]]: A skill added by the [[Online:Summerset (Chapter)|Summerset]] chapter which allows the crafting and improvement of [[Online:Jewelry|Jewelry]]. *[[Online:Provisioning|Provisioning]]: The art of converting [[Online:Provisioning Ingredients|Ingredients]] into ingestible [[Online:Food Recipes|Foods]] and [[Online:Beverage Recipes|Drinks]]. *[[Online:Woodworking|Woodworking]]: The art of converting [[Online:Woodworking Materials|raw wood]] into and improving upon [[Online:Staves|Staves]], [[Online:Bows|Bows]], and [[Online:Shields|Shields]]. ===Skill points=== The table below shows the amount of [[Online:Skills|skill points]] required in order to max out each profession skill line. {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! Order!! Profession !! Skill points required |- | 1 || Alchemy || 21 |- | 2 || Blacksmithing || 26 |- | 3 || Clothing || 26 |- | 4 || Enchanting || 23 |- | 5 || Jewelry Crafting || 18 |- | 6 || Provisioning || 25 |- | 7 || Woodworking || 26 |-class="sortbottom" |'''Totals:'''||'''All'''||'''165''' |} ==Crafting Stations== [[File:ON-place-The Ringing Anvil.jpg|thumb|right|A blacksmithing station]] Crafting Stations are places at which you can partake in the crafting professions. Each type of crafting station is most commonly found at a particular type of [[Online:Stores|store]]: alchemy stations are found at [[Online:Apothecaries|apothecaries]], blacksmithing stations are found at [[Online:Smithies|smithies]], clothing stations are found at smithies and [[Online:Clothiers|clothiers]], enchanting stations are found at [[Online:Chironasia|chironasia]], and woodworking stations are found at [[Online:Carpentries|carpentries]] and some smithies. Cooking fires for provisioning are most commonly found in [[Online:Inns|inns]] and [[Online:Camps|camps]]. Jewelry crafting stations are inconsistently placed, but can usually be found in major cities. You can also have crafting stations in your home. [[ON:Services_Furnishings/Crafting_Stations#Standard_Crafting_Stations|Standard ones]] are obtainable in various ways. There are also different specialized crafting stations: # Around the world, you can find special [[Online:Crafting Sites|Crafting Sites]] that are equipped with blacksmithing, clothing, jewelry, and woodworking stations for crafting items in specific [[Online:Sets#Craftable_Sets|Sets]]. At each site, the stations there can be used to craft the Set for that location or as normal crafting stations. # You can obtain Attunable Crafting Station furnishings (perhaps by buying with Writ Vouchers, or via Guild Stores), go to one of the sites described in 1, and attune your stations to that Set. Then you can have stations in your home that can craft that Set. This attunement can only be done once, it is permanent. # You can obtain a Grand Master Crafting Station furnishing (from [[ON:Faustina_Curio|Faustina Curio]]), feed Attuned Crafting Stations into it, and thereby have a station that can craft in a variety of sets. All Blacksmithing, clothing, and woodworking stations craft items with specific [[Online:Styles|styles]]. A style can be used if the corresponding [[Online:Crafting Motifs|crafting motif]] is known for that item. The [[Online:Crafting Station Style Order|order that crafting stations list the available styles]] is unfortunately not obvious. ==Refinement== After being harvested from resource nodes, raw materials for four different crafting professions (blacksmithing, clothing, jewelry crafting, and woodworking) may be refined, 10 at a time, into 7-10 refined craftable items, averaging an 85% recovery rate. For instance, if a player were to refine 10,000 raw blacksmithing ores, they could expect to get an average of 8,500 refined items. In addition to craftable items, refining raw materials will also yield trait items and upgrading items, which can improve the quality crafted items (such as armor, weapons, or jewelry). At the maximum skill level of the "extraction" skill for each profession, the likelihood is as follows (the same between all professions): {|class=wikitable !rowspan=2|Temper/Tannin/Plating/Resin quality !!colspan=5|% chance per raw material |- !Extraction 0 !Extraction 1 !Extraction 2 !Extraction 3 !Ext 3 +
[[ON:Champion#Craft|Meticulous Disassembly]] |- |{{ESO Quality Color|f|Fine}} || 1.00%{{huh}} || 1.15%{{huh}} || 1.31%{{huh}} || 1.50% || 1.69% |- |{{ESO Quality Color|s|Superior}} || 0% || 0.96%{{huh}} || 1.09%{{huh}} || 1.25% || 1.41% |- |{{ESO Quality Color|e|Epic}} || 0% || 0% || 0.66%{{huh}} || 0.75% || 0.84% |- |{{ESO Quality Color|l|Legendary}} || 0% || 0% || 0% || 0.50% || 0.56% |} Each increased level of the relevant extraction skill (Metal Extraction, Unraveling, Jewelry Extraction, and Wood Extraction) as well as the [[ON:Champion|Champion]] Craft perk [[ON:Champion#Craft|Meticulous Disassembly]] seem to increase the chance of getting improvement materials by 12.5% past the previous skill/perk level. These appear interchangeable; for instance, if a player had Extraction 2 and Meticulous Disassembly, it would be equivalent to having Extraction 3. Note that this is not the chance of getting a single upgrading material or the chance of getting any number of upgrading materials, but an averaged drop rate over a long period of time. For instance, if a player with fully leveled Extraction skills, but without Meticulous Disassembly, were to refine 10,000 raw blacksmithing ores, they could expect to get an average of 150 {{ESO Quality Color|f|Honing Stone}}, 125 {{ESO Quality Color|s|Dwarven Oil}}, 75 {{ESO Quality Color|e|Grain Solvent}}, and 50 {{ESO Quality Color|l|Tempering Alloy}}. ==Certification== Seven skills in ESO are eligible for [[Online:Crafting Certification|Certification]]. Completing the certification quests enables access to repeatable [[Online:Crafting Writs|Crafting Writs]] quests. When you reach level six a new notice will appear on the noticeboards in all major cities. The notice states that master crafters are willing to share their knowledge on crafting for free, which will allow you to complete writs. There are two master crafters, [[Online:Millenith|Millenith]] and [[Online:Danel Telleno|Danel Telleno]], who can certify you in three professions each. With the [[Online:Summerset (Chapter)|Summerset]] chapter, the seventh skill - [[ON:Jewelry Crafting|Jewelry Crafting]] - was added. It can only be learned from [[ON:Felarian|Felarian]] and [[Online:Jewelry Crafting Certification|his associated quest]] in [[ON:Alinor|Alinor]], which requires the chapter to visit. ==Crafting Writs== *''[[ON:Crafting Writs|See main article]]'' ==Inspiration== All seven crafting professions use [[File:ON-icon-Inspiration.png|link=]] '''Inspiration''' for [[Online:leveling|leveling]] purposes. Inspiration is gained from performing crafting activities, such as creation, improvement, extraction, and refinement, as well as by completing [[#Crafting Writs|writs]]. You can increase the amount of inspiration you earn in a few ways. 45 [[ON:Champion|Champion Points]] can be allocated in the Craft skill tree towards the [[ON:Inspiration Boost|Inspiration Boost]] passive perk, increasing gains by 30%. Online:Enchanting:
{{Trail|Crafting}} {{/Progression}} [[File:ON-misc-Enchanting Example.png|thumb|left|Enchanting is a crafting skill of combining runes to create glyphs, which are then used to enchant weapons, armor and jewelry.]] '''Enchanting''' is a [[Online:Crafting|crafting]] profession in ''[[Online:Online|Elder Scrolls Online]]''. You can use it to combine [[Online:Runestones|Runestones]] into [[ON:Glyphs|Glyphs]], which add magical effects to [[ON:Weapons|weapons]], [[ON:Armor|armor]] and [[ON:Jewelry|jewelry]]. Once you are [[ON:Crafting_Certification|Certified]] in this craft, you will have access to repeatable [[ON:Crafting_Writs|Crafting Writ quests]]. In addition to glyphs, the Enchanting skill allows you to craft [[ON:Furnishing Praxes|furnishings]] for your home. {{FMI}} {{NewLeft}} __TOC__ == Learning == The Enchanting skill line is granted the first time you activate an enchanting station. === Gaining Inspiration === Experience gained in a craft is called "inspiration". *Inspiration can be gained by [[ON:Enchanting#Creating_Glyphs|Creating Glyphs]], [[ON:Enchanting#Deconstructing_Glyphs|Deconstructing Glyphs]], translating [[ON:Enchanting#Online:Runestones|Runestones]], completing [[ON:Enchanter_Writ|Enchanter Writs]] or [[ON:A Masterful Glyph|Master Writs]], or reading [[ON:Skill Books|Skill Books]]. *The skill books which increase Enchanting are: **[[ON:Ahzidal's Descent|Ahzidal's Descent]] **[[ON:Enigma of the Runestones|Enigma of the Runestones]] **[[ON:Glyphs and Enchantment|Glyphs and Enchantment]] **[[ON:Harvest's End|Harvest's End]] **[[ON:A Request for Relief|A Request for Relief]] *The amount of inspiration gained from completing writs is based entirely on the potency level required by the writ and is detailed on the [[ON:Enchanter_Writ|Enchanter Writs]] page. *The amount of inspiration gained from [[ON:Enchanting#Creating_Glyphs|Creating Glyphs]], and [[ON:Enchanting#Deconstructing_Glyphs|Deconstructing Glyphs]] is based on your current enchanting skill level as well as the level and quality of the glyph. *Deconstructing a glyph made by other characters (alts included) gives more inspiration than deconstructing a glyph made by you. Such glyphs can be readily found at [[ON:Guild Kiosks|Guild Kiosks]], in treasure chests and [[ON:Safebox|Safeboxes]], and other sources. *Deconstructing a glyph made with the {{Item Link|id=45851|Jejota}} rune gives about twice as much inspiration as a glyph made with {{Item Link|id=45850|Ta}}. Deconstructing a glyph made with the {{Item Link|id=45852|Denata}} rune gives the same Inspiration as a glyph made with {{Item Link|id=45853|Rekuta}}, about 50% more than a glyph made with {{Item Link|id=45851|Jejota}}. Finally, a glyph made with {{Item Link|id=45854|Kuta}} gives about 15% more inspiration than a glyph made with {{Item Link|id=45852|Denata}} or {{Item Link|id=45853|Rekuta}}. Therefore, if purchasing glyphs for deconstruction, it may be more cost effective to focus only on Superior quality glyphs made with {{Item Link|id=45852|Denata}} runes. *Deconstructing a glyph made with the {{Item Link|id=68341|Repora}} or {{Item Link|id=68340|Itade}} CP 160 runes, give more inspiration than deconstructing a glyph made with any CP 150 [[ON:Runestones#Potency_Runes|Potency Rune]]. For example: deconstructing a {{ESO Quality Color|b|'''Common''' (white)}} glyph, not made by you, with a {{Item Link|id=68341|Repora}} and a {{Item Link|id=45850|Ta}}, with the +20% [[ON:Inspiration Boost|Inspiration Boost]] passive champion unlock, will gain you 4569 inspiration at any level. === Inspiration Required by Level === Each level has a specific amount of Inspiration required before advancing to the next level as detailed in the table below. Good luck."'' {{NewLine}} == Skill Usage == ===Finding Runes=== In order to create an enchantment, you need three different types of [[Online:Runestones|runestone]]. These are Potency, Essence, and Aspect. Runestones can be harvested from nodes as you travel through the world, extracted from glyphs, or received in mail if you have the Hireling perks. [[ON:Enchanters|Enchanters]] also sell Potency runes for gold. [[File:ON-node-Runestone.jpg|thumb|right|A runestone node]] {| class="wikitable" |- ! Type of Runestone !! Icon color !! Icon shape !! Examples |- | [[Online:Runestones#Potency_Runes|Potency]] || Blue || Square || {{icon|r|Jora}} {{icon|r|Notade}} {{icon|r|Kedeko}} |- | [[Online:Runestones#Essence_Runes|Essence]] || Yellow/green || Hexagonal || {{icon|r|Dekeipa}} {{icon|r|Kaderi}} {{icon|r|Oru}} |- | [[Online:Runestones#Aspect_Runes|Aspect]] || Red || Circular || {{icon|r|Ta}} {{icon|r|Jejota}} {{icon|r|Rekuta}} |} {{NewLine}} A single runestone provides multiple runes of different types. Essence and Aspect runes of all kinds can drop in all zones. Potency runes drop half of the time based on your level and the other half based on your rank in the Potency Improvement skill. === Creating Glyphs === While standing at an Enchanter's table, you combine one Potency, one Essence, and one Aspect runestone to make a Glyph. Unlike [[Online:Provisioning|Provisioning]], you do not need a recipe. If your character doesn't already know what the runestones do, you will learn their effects while creating the Glyph. The title and icon of the Glyph will tell you if it is for weapons, armor, or jewelry. {| class="wikitable" |- ! Type of Glyph !! Icon color !! Icon shape !! Examples |- | [[ON:Weapons|Weapon]] || Bronze || Pentagonal || {{icon|g|weapon-Glyph of Frost}} {{icon|g|weapon-Glyph of Absorb Stamina}} {{icon|g|weapon-Glyph of Absorb Health}} |- | [[ON:Armor|Armor]] || Silver || Reuleaux triangle || {{icon|g|armor-Glyph of Stamina}} {{icon|g|armor-Glyph of Magicka}} {{icon|g|armor-Glyph of Health}} |- | [[ON:Jewelry|Jewelry]] || Gold || Circular || {{icon|g|jewelry-Glyph of Frost Resist}} {{icon|g|jewelry-Glyph of Disease Resist}} {{icon|g|jewelry-Glyph of Magicka Recovery}} |} Note that you must use a Potency runestone of the correct level for the item which you wish to enchant. For example, if you wish to enchant a level 10 weapon with a Glyph of Frost, you must use a Potency rune which covers level 10. There are three possibilities, Jora (level 1-10), Porade (level 5-15), and Jera (level 10-20). Obviously the highest strength Glyph will be created from the highest level Potency rune. === Applying Glyphs === While you must be at an Enchanter's table in order to create a Glyph, you do not need any special equipment in order to enchant an item with the Glyph in your possession. You simply select the item you wish to enchant in the Inventory screen, and choose "Enchant". The Glyph you have must be of the correct type and an appropriate level for the item to be enchanted. Glyphs may be applied to equipment which is of the same or higher level, but higher-level glyphs may not be applied to lower-level equipment. You may, for example, apply a Simple glyph to a Level 50/CP160 Rubedite piece of equipment, but you cannot apply an Average glyph to Level 14 Iron gear. Note that any quality of Glyph may be applied to any quality of item, however. You could put a {{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Legendary'''}} quality Glyph on a {{ESO Quality Color|b|'''Base'''}} quality item if you wanted to. While glyphs may not be removed once they have been applied, enchantments may be changed. For example, an armor piece with an increased Magicka recovery rate enchantment can be changed to a increased Health enchantment by applying an appropriate glyph. By the same token, a sword with a fire damage enchantment can be given a frost damage enchantment by applying an appropriate glyph. '''Special note about Armor Glyphs:''' Only Head, Chest, Legs, and Shields receive the full effect of an enchantment. [[File:ON-misc-Alchemy_Table_Example.png|thumb|left|Creating potions in ESO involves combining 1 solvent with 2-3 reagents at the alchemy table.]]{{TOCright}}
'''Alchemy''' is a [[Online:Crafting|crafting]] profession in ''[[Online:Online|Elder Scrolls Online]]''. You can use it to create many types of potions and poisons. You must be at an alchemist's lab in order to create any items. In general, potions provide you with a quick boost to {{ESO Health Link}}, {{ESO Stamina Link}}, {{ESO Magicka Link}}, as well as other beneficial effects. Poisons were introduced in Update 10 and can be applied to your weapon, nullifying any [[ON:Enchanting|enchantments]] but providing powerful additional effects.

Once you are [[ON:Crafting_Certification|Certified]] in this craft, you will have access to repeatable [[ON:Crafting_Writs|Crafting Writ quests]].

Alchemy works similarly to previous games in the series, in that you do not need to find alchemy recipes before attempting to make potions. You are also able to eat potion [[ON:Alchemy Ingredients|ingredients]] to discover their first effect.  Otherwise, you can try putting multiple ingredients with unknown effects together to learn their properties.

Making potions has been refined since Skyrim, and now requires two or three [[Online:Reagents|reagents]] plus a [[Online:Alchemy Ingredients#Solvents|solvent]]. Using a more powerful solvent boosts the power of your potion.  A water-based solvent creates a potion that you can drink to receive its effects, while an oil-based solvent creates poisons which can be applied to your weapons to cause negative effects on your enemies.  While potions can be crafted in batches of 1-4, poisons are created in batches of 4-16 samples (depending on your [[ON:Chemistry|Chemistry]] passive).

In general, you want to avoid negative effects when making potions, as these will only have undesirable effects.  The [[ON:Snakeblood|Snakeblood]] passive mitigates these effects, but it's better to simply avoid them in the first place whenever possible.  In poisons, all effects can be useful - negative effects will harm or debilitate your targets while positive ones will do the same to a lesser degree but also benefit you.  Poison can be applied to any weapon, including Staves.  Using a poison on a weapon will override its [[ON:Enchanting|Enchantment]] until the poison has been depleted.  Each strike has a 20% chance of triggering the poison's effect, reducing the poison charge on the weapon by one when it does so.

In addition to potions and poisons, the Alchemy skill allows you to craft [[ON:Furnishing Formulae|furnishings]] for your home.
{{NewLeft}}
== Learning ==
The Alchemy skill line is granted the first time you activate an alchemy station.  You can increase your skill by crafting potions and poisons, learning all of the various effects for every reagent, and by completing [[ON:Alchemist Writ|Alchemist Writ]]s or [[ON:A Masterful Concoction|Master Writs]].  In addition, you can earn free levels in the skill line by reading [[ON:Skill Books|Skill Books]], which may be found randomly on bookshelves anywhere.  The skill books which increase Alchemy are:
*[[ON:Alchemy Practicum|Alchemy Practicum]]
*[[ON:Alchemy: Discovering Traits|Alchemy: Discovering Traits]]
*[[ON:Confessions of a Bold Alchemist|Confessions of a Bold Alchemist]]
*[[ON:Fundaments of Alchemy|Fundaments of Alchemy]]
*[[ON:Of the Dragonfires (Fragment)|Of the Dragonfires (Fragment)]]
*[[ON:Sep's Kiss|Sep's Kiss]]

== Alchemist Dialogue ==
You can learn about this profession by speaking with some of the alchemists.
:'''How does alchemy work exactly?''' 
:''"Alchemy is the art of creating potions. We scour the fields and caves of [[Online:Tamriel|Tamriel]] in search of reagents like mushrooms, flowers, and the like. Mixing these ingredients with a water solvent in the correct quantities can create powerful elixirs."''
:'''Plants and water? That's it?'''
:''"Well, not just any water will do. You'll find that some pools of water contain special qualities that make them ideal for potion-making. The grade of the water determines the potency of the product."''
:'''Does it matter what reagents I use?'''
:''"All reagents have hidden properties. When they are combined with other ingredients that bestow the same benefits, the potency is compounded. This reaction determines the nature of the potion. It's just a matter of experimentation, you see?"''

==Formulae==
===Two Reagents===
In ESO, two [[ON:Alchemy Ingredients|reagents]] with the same effect need to be combined in order to craft a potion. Be aware that when crafting potions, some combinations will provide a not always beneficial side effect.  The [[ON:Snakeblood|Snakeblood]] passive will reduce (or with 3 points even eliminate) the negative side-effects, but it's better to simply avoid them if possible.  All effects in poisons are negative, so there's no need to worry about unintended side-effects with poisons, though poisons with multiple effects will have the duration of all effects reduced.  Remember that you have to also provide a solvent, which influences the strength, but not the effect, of a potion. As of Update 51, there are 270 two-reagent combinations.

{{ON:Alchemy/Two Reagent Formulae}}

===Three Reagents===
Learning the Ability ''[[ON:Laboratory Use|Laboratory Use]]'' enables you to use of up to three reagents. This opens the door to a large variety of multi-effect potions since each effect has to be present only two times within the reagents chosen in order to be applied to a potion. Listing all possible formulae for potions with three reagents would be rather pointless (there are 5962 such formulae as of Update 51) - those interested can use [http://esolog.uesp.net/viewPotions.php ESO Alchemy Calculator]. To use three reagents to their full potential, you also need to understand how opposing effects work. See the ''[[ON:Laboratory Use|Laboratory Use]]'' page for more details.

360 of the three-reagent formulae produce '''three effects''' (the primary one, which gives name to the resulting potion, and '''two''' secondaries). These formulae are listed below.

The materials refine into the following: {{Online:Tailoring}} ===Crafting new items=== Clothing allows you to create cloth armor (light) or leather armor (medium). Initially you can craft from Jute and Hide, but when you improve your Clothing skill and apply skill points towards Tailoring, you get access to higher tier materials. For each material you can create items with a range of armor values and level requirements, depending on how much material you choose to use. Once you have access to a material, you can create every item out of it. See [[Online:Clothing Materials|this page]] for the full list of the cloth and leather used in Clothing. To craft a new item, you must choose the type of the item (robe, hat, etc.), the type and quantity of the material to use, the [[Online:Clothing#Style|style]] of the item to create (this is required, and every style requires a specific secondary ingredient), and optionally a [[Online:Clothing#Traits|trait]] to add among the traits you have unlocked for this specific item type (adding a trait requires a tertiary ingredient). ===Deconstructing items=== You can deconstruct a piece of armor at a clothing station. The process destroys the item, but allows the recovery of refined materials, secondary (style) or tertiary (trait) ingredients that were used to create this item, and the extraction of a tannin of the item's quality. The chances of extracting each material are calculated separately, and are improved with higher ranks of the Unravelling skill. Finally, you will always get some Clothing experience, but much less will be obtained from deconstructing an item you made yourself. ===Improving items=== At a clothing station, you can apply [[Online:Clothing Materials#Tannins|tannins]] to items to try and improve them. Each improvement has only a chance of success, the higher the tier of the item the smaller the chance. Tannins can be obtained when refining raw fibers and scraps. ===Research=== Having an item with a [[Online:Clothing#Traits|trait]], you can learn how to create other items of the same type with the same trait. Research takes predefined time and destroys the item. For a given item type researching the first trait lasts 6 hours, and each next trait takes twice longer than the previous. You can only research one trait per profession at a time; however, each profession has a perk (for Clothing it is Stitching) that allows you to have two or three parallel research processes. Traits on different types of items are completely separate, so if you learned a trait on a robe you can only apply it to a robe and not to a hat, and time for researching a trait for a robe will only depend on how many traits you have already discovered for a robe. ==Style== {{ON:Styles}} ==Traits== A weapon or piece of armor can have a single trait (in addition to an enchantment). These traits can be [[Online:Clothing#Clothing Stations|researched]] at crafting stations from an existing item which possesses the trait, destroying the item in the process. To add a trait when crafting one must use a tertiary ingredient. {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! Trait (Armor) !! Material !! Description |- | Sturdy || {{icon|trait material|Quartz|24}} Quartz || Give a 22% chance to avoid decay when wielder is defeated |- | Impenetrable || {{icon|trait material|Diamond|24}} Diamond || Increases resistance to Critical hits by 60 |- | Reinforced || {{icon|trait material|Sardonyx|24}} Sardonyx || Increases this item's Armor value by 4% |- | Well-fitted || {{icon|trait material|Almandine|24}} Almandine || Reduces the cost of Sprinting by 2% |- | Training || {{icon|trait material|Emerald|24}} Emerald || Increases armor skill line experience with this armor type by 11% |- | Infused || {{icon|trait material|Bloodstone|24}} Bloodstone || Increases this item's armor enchantment effect by 8% |- | Exploration || {{icon|trait material|Garnet|24}} Garnet || Increases exploration experience gained by 6% |- | Divines || {{icon|trait material|Sapphire|24}} Sapphire || Increases Mundus Stone effects by 4% |} == Achievements == There are a number of achievements associated with Clothing. {{/Achievements}} {{Online Skills}} [[Category:Online-Skill Lines]][[Category:Online-Skill Lines-Crafting]]

{{Trail|Crafting}} {{/Progression}} '''Blacksmithing''' is a [[Online:Crafting|crafting]] profession in ''[[Online:Online|Elder Scrolls Online]]''. This profession's specialty is to create and improve [[Online:Heavy Armor|heavy armor]] and metal [[Online:Weapons|weapons]] in various styles of different races. To create a weapon or a piece of armor you need to be at a [[ON:Blacksmithing Station|blacksmithing station]]. Such stations are also used to conduct research on different kinds of heavy armor and metal weapons traits. The list of ingredients (ores, ingots, and tempers) used in Blacksmithing can be found [[Online:Blacksmithing Materials|here]]. Once you are [[ON:Crafting_Certification|Certified]] in this craft, you will have access to repeatable [[ON:Crafting_Writs|Crafting Writ quests]]. In addition to armor and weapons, the Blacksmithing skill allows you to craft [[ON:Furnishing Diagrams|furnishings]] for your home. == Learning == The Blacksmithing skill line is granted the first time you activate a blacksmithing station. You can increase your skill by crafting or deconstructing armor and weapons, researching traits, and by completing [[ON:Blacksmith Writ|Blacksmith Writ]]s or [[ON:A Masterful Plate|Master]] [[ON:A Masterful Weapon (Blacksmithing)|Writs]]. In addition, you can earn free levels in the skill line by reading [[ON:Skill Books|Skill Books]], which may be found randomly on bookshelves anywhere. The skill books which increase Blacksmithing are: *[[ON:Smithing: A Worthy Endeavor|Smithing: A Worthy Endeavor]] *[[ON:Heavy Armor: A Forge-Wife's Advice|Heavy Armor: A Forge-Wife's Advice]] *[[ON:The Book of Circles: Forging Maxims|The Book of Circles: Forging Maxims]] *[[ON:Nord Armorers and Armsmen|Nord Armorers and Armsmen]] *[[ON:Treatise on Metallurgical Anomalies|Treatise on Metallurgical Anomalies]] == Blacksmith Dialogue == You can learn about this profession by speaking with some of the blacksmiths. :'''I'd like to learn more about blacksmithing.''' :''"We put hammer to anvil to forge [[Online:Armor|armor]] and weapons. This requires a lot of metal. We scour hills and caves looking for rare ores to work.
Raw materials will only take you so far. You need [[Online:Crafting Motifs|style books]] and special ingredients for more advanced work."'' :'''I'm sure there's a lot to learn''' :''"You bet. A true blacksmith can read the metal to determine its potential. During the forging process we can choose a [[ON:Traits|trait]] that best fits the item—provided we've done our [[ON:Traits#Research|research]]. Additional sharpening, extra weight … these are just examples."'' :'''Is there more to it?''' :''"Well, the piece can be augmented even more through the use of tempers. These elements can enhance the value and quality of your work. Of course, no worthwhile endeavor comes without risk. Fall Resistance doesn't exist, though some bonuses can reduce your Fall Damage taken. (Fall Damage isn't a damage type per-se, it is in its own category (see [[#Note|Note]])) *Non-player sourced damage types:
Those damage types aren't like the usual previous damage types. The game almost never mentions them, they have unique properties and some of them are found only in very precise scenarios. **"Generic Damage", which is actually found in many places with [[ON:Traps|Traps]] and NPCs sometimes dealing it. It is theorized to be a placeholder damage type until it is changed into a regular damage type in the development, but devs sometimes forget to change it. Generic Damage is reduced by damage taken reduction effects and by your Generic Resistance which is the highest between your {{ESO Resistance Link|Physical|||y}} and {{ESO Resistance Link|Spell}}. **"Drown Damage", which is found in [[ON:Slaughterfish|Slaughterfish]], [[ON:Traps#Abyssal Assault/Exsanguinating Ichor|Abyssal Assault]], the "Exsanguinating Ichor" area in [[ON:Runemaster's Acropolis|Runemaster's Acropolis]] and [[ON:Traps#Drowning|Drowning]] [[ON:Beneath the Abecean Sea|Beneath the Abecean Sea]]. This is not reduced by your damage taken reduction effects, and it bypasses your damage shields. Players have 0 Drown Resistance. The first three hazards negate all your healing taken with [[ON:Combat#Combat Effects|Heal Absorption]]. **"Earth Damage", which is found in [[ON:Sihadid#Notes|Sihadid]]'s "Sands of Awakening" attack, [[ON:Domihaus the Bloody-Horned|Domihaus the Bloody-Horned]] Stone Totem's "Slam" attack and in the [[ON:Corruption of Stone|Corruption of Stone]]'s "Unstable Explosion". It is also found in the Boulder Bash effect gained by completing a Boulder Dash oddity in the [[ON:Night_Market|Night Market]]. It is theorized to be a very early damage type that was deprecated, but its recent (and unexpected) re-appearance in the [[ON:Night_Market|Night Market]] gently pushes against this notion. Earth Damage is reduced by damage taken reduction effects and by your Earth Resistance which is the highest between your {{ESO Resistance Link|Physical|||y}} and {{ESO Resistance Link|Spell}}. **"None Damage", which is found in the Imperial Law hazard when approaching a [[ON:Dremora Channeler|Dremora Channeler]] on a Cyrodiil bridge to the Imperial City. Due to the erratic damage numbers of this hazard it has not been determined if it is or isn't reduced by your armor and damage taken reduction effects, and if it bypasses damage shields. **"Daedric Weapon Damage", which is the damage taken when [[ON:Volendrung|Volendrung]]'s bar is fully depleted. It deals 100% of the wielder's {{ESO Health Link|Max}} + 1 damage. There is no protection against it and it bypasses your damage shields. Online:Stealth:
{{Trail|Combat}} '''Stealth''', also known as '''Sneak''', governs your ability to escape detection by others through reducing your visibility and noisiness. It is primarily useful for evading confrontation with enemies, and for executing surprise attacks that inflict critical damage. In previous Elder Scrolls games, "Stealth" and "Sneak" are different concepts: stealth being a grouping of (more-or-less loosely) conceptually related skills, of which sneak was one. In ESO, there is not a distinct, developed skill line for this behavior, and any character can sneak. Similarly, being "stealthed" in ESO usually refers to a sneaking character who is hidden from enemies. ==Skill Usage== Toggling the [[Online:Controls#Sneak|sneak control]] causes the player to crouch or stand, indicating that you have entered or left sneak mode. Moving while sneaking will burn stamina; if the player stops moving, stamina regenerates normally. While sneaking, the crosshair becomes a special "eye" reticle indicating the following statuses: {| {{AL|M}} |{{Image Overlay|ON-icon-achievement-Blank.png|ON-icon-stealth-Hidden.png|32px}} A horizontal line indicates you are completely hidden, or "stealthed". This is accompanied by the text HIDDEN, and your character gains a shadow over their location. In this state, a successful pickpocket won't incur a bounty. |- |{{Image Overlay|ON-icon-achievement-Blank.png|ON-icon-stealth-Danger.png|32px}} The "eye" begins to open as you get near to a potential witness, or if an NPC begins to search for you. A partially-open "eye" with the text "HIDDEN" means you are hidden, as long as you do nothing to break stealth (i.e.--pickpocket, assault). The eye can also begin to open if you get near an enemy that can see through your Stealth/disguise. A red stealth eye is seen above the enemy and a "DANGER" is displayed above your stealth eye instead of "HIDDEN". |- |{{Image Overlay|ON-icon-achievement-Blank.png|ON-icon-stealth-Detected.png|32px}} A solid oval means that somebody knows where you are or can see you. This is accompanied by the text "DETECTED". Note that you will also see this icon and text whenever interacting with objects even if there are no witnesses around to see you. |} === Sneak Attacks === You perform a sneak attack when you physically strike someone who is unaware of your presence. Sneak attacks stun the targets hit, unless they are under the influence of a [[ON:Radiant Magelight|Radiant Magelight]]. * The sneak multiplier is only applied to the physical damage done by a weapon, i.e. the damage shown for the weapon in your inventory. ** [[Online:Poison Damage|Poison]] and [[Online:Enchanting|enchantment]]-related damage enhancements are added to damage inflicted by power attacks, their effects are not increased by performing sneak attacks * Sneak damage applies to all attack types, including dual-wield weapons, bows, and skills. If a sneak attack does not kill an enemy, you will become detected -- by the enemy themselves and by any of their allies within detection range. This seems to be true even if it does not appear that the enemies "ought" to be able to know where the attack came from -- e.g., by an arrow fired from cover. Also, when you attack from sneak, you immediately leave sneak. Leaving sneak automatically has the benefit of making you instantly able to attack/defend/run without being handicapped in your movement speed, but may factor into the fact that you become immediately visible. Subsequently crouching to return to sneak, or using concealing skills such as the Nightblade's Shadow Cloak, will have whatever success in hiding you again that they would in any combat situation: mixed, depending on your circumstances. However, if you can regain sneak, you can immediately attack again and have the usual sneak multipliers apply. [[File:ON-icon-misc-Reveal.png|right]] === Sneak Suppression === Sometimes your ability to sneak is suppressed. There are various things that can cause this: *An NPC guard with a lamp, found in places associated with the [[ON:Thieves Guild|Thieves Guild]], [[ON:Dark Brotherhood|Dark Brotherhood]], or [[ON:Morrowind|Morrowind]] DLCs. While sneaking, you will see a shining circle on the ground around them. You cannot sneak within this circle, and possibly for a few seconds after leaving it. If you are in a restricted area or have a bounty on your head, the guard will generally try to arrest or attack you if you are spotted. *Some traps in these same areas can temporarily inhibit your ability to sneak. Try to keep an eye out for any trip wires or leaky pots which can explode and deal damage in addition to suppressing your stealth. *In PVP zones, other players may use a Potion or Poison with the [[ON:Detection|Detection]] trait against you, preventing you from entering stealth unless you can [[ON:Cleansing|purge]] the effect somehow. *The [[ON:Expert Hunter|Expert Hunter]], [[ON:Magelight|Magelight]], [[ON:Piercing Mark|Piercing Mark]], [[ON:Revealing Flare|Revealing Flare]] and [[ON:Soul Strike|Soul Strike]] abilities can also inhibit stealth in PVP areas. (You may also use these abilities to detect NPCs who are using stealth, though these are also much more common in PVP zones.) *The [[ON:Way of Air|Way of Air]] and [[ON:Sentry (set)|Sentry]] sets give bonuses that increase the wearer's stealth detection radius. * You will not be able to sneak while wearing a disguise, which can be done for certain quests. Instead, a message will display stating that sneaking would cause suspicion. * You cannot sneak normally in [[ON:Werewolf|Werewolf]] form, though sources which give [[ON:Invisibility|Invisibility]] still work. ==Sneak Buffs== Sneak is improved by buffs such as a decrease in the distance at which you can be detected, an increase of the damage from stealth, a reduction of its cost and other bonuses. ===Skills=== {|class=sortable wikitable border="1" ! Online:Crafting Writs:
{{Trail|Quests|nocat=1}}[[Category:Online-Crafting]][[Category:Online-Quests| ]] '''Crafting Writs''' are repeatable quests available to any [[#Certification|certified]] crafter who is at least level 6. Crafting Writs can be accepted from writs boards located in major towns and cities. Accepting a writ begins an associated quest. Successful completion of a crafting writ will reward experience, gold, a consumable box of supplies, and [[ON:Crafting#Inspiration|inspiration]] for that profession. One writ for each profession may be completed per day. As of [[Online:Update 37|Update 37]], daily writs reset at 3am UTC on EU [[Online:Megaservers|servers]], and 10am UTC on NA servers. ==Locations== {{Online:Crafting Writ Boards}} ==Certification== To accept crafting writs, you must first become certified in your chosen professions. The certification process involves a short quest where you are required to craft an item for a master crafter NPC, and serves as a tutorial to the crafting systems. If you are already an established crafter, and have reached Rank 10 in a particular crafting skill line, you can skip the tutorial section and become certified immediately. All certifications require the character to be at least level 6. *{{Quest Link|Crafting Certification}} **{{Quest Link|Alchemist Certification}} **{{Quest Link|Blacksmith Certification}} **{{Quest Link|Clothier Certification}} **{{Quest Link|Enchanter Certification}} **{{Quest Link|Jewelry Crafting Certification}} (this certification requires access to Alinor in Summerset) **{{Quest Link|Provisioner Certification}} **{{Quest Link|Woodworker Certification}} ==Normal Writs== The following is a list of daily crafting writ quests that can be picked up at writ boards. These writs are relatively straightforward and inexpensive to complete. Arms and armor are always requested at the lowest quality, with no additional trait and can be created at regular [[ON:Crafting Stations|Crafting Stations]]. ===Consumables Crafting Writs=== When activating the Consumables Crafting Writs board, you'll be greeted with: :''"
"Certified Crafters, We Want Your Wares! Potions, Glyphs, Food, and Drink! Hone your craft and earn a reward!""'' *{{Quest Link|Alchemist Writ}} *{{Quest Link|Enchanter Writ}} *{{Quest Link|Provisioner Writ}} ===Equipment Crafting Writs=== When activating the Equipment Crafting Writs board, you'll be greeted with: :'''' All alliance zones give you the same message from your sovereign, even if you're in an enemy alliance zone. :{{ESO DC}}''"King Emeric offers greetings! Masters of the craft await you in Daggerfall! Free training for all new to their craft; certification for accomplished crafters! All at no cost to you, citizen!"'' :{{ESO AD}} {{huh}} :{{ESO EP}} {{huh}} The message in neutral zones give messages from the locals, with a few exceptions... :{{ESO DLC|Thieves Guild}}(Same as alliance message) :{{ESO MW}}''"Lord Vivec gives greetings! Masters of the craft await you in Vivec City. We offer training for all new to their craft, and certification for accomplished crafters. Free for all citizens!"'' :{{ESO SS}}''"Queen Ayrenn bids you welcome! Masters of the craft await you in Alinor! New crafters shall be trained! Accomplished crafters will be certified!
