Online:Artifacts: {{Trail|addcat1=Items|Styles}} {{split|PvP artifacts need to be split for the purpose of better organising skill lines}} '''Artifacts''' are unique and powerful items which grant their owners special abilities. Many of these items have been [[Lore:Artifacts|seen in other games in the franchise]]. In the context of Elder Scrolls Online, artifacts are seen occasionally during quests or can be temporarily obtained in PvP. The [[ON:Styles|visual style]] of several artifacts can also be applied to your weapons via the [[ON:Outfit System|Outfit System]]. Some weapon and apparel artifacts are seen and can theoretically be used by players, but are unavailable to be obtained. ==Artifact Styles== [[File:ON-crown store-Chrysamere.jpg|thumb|Chrysamere, one of many Artifact styles]] *''Main page: [[Online:Artifact Styles|Artifact Styles]]'' {{NewLine}} ==Artifact Weapons== :''The chaos of Cyrodiil reaches frantic new heights with the arrival of Artifact Weapons!'' :''For reasons that no sane person can possibly fathom, the Daedric Prince of Madness Sheogorath seems intent on prolonging the conflict in Cyrodiil. To that end, he occasionally sends weapons of great power to Tamriel. Players who take up these weapons have their standard ability bar icons replaced by a suite of new and terrifying Artifact abilities! But these abilities-like all gifts from Sheogorath—come at a cost. Players must feed the weapon Alliance Points to maintain their hold on it. These Alliance Points are tracked in a unique meter found in the player Ul. Points acquired from sources other than quests and repairing structures will fuel the weapon. If the meter is fully depleted, however, the weapon turns on the wielder, killing them and stripping them of their Artifact powers.'' :''Players wishing to experience the power of Artifact Weapons in a less competitive atmosphere can do so in Cheesemonger's Hollow—one of Sheogorath's pocket realms. Portals to this bizarre testing ground exist at the Northern Morrowind Gate, Southern High Rock Gate, and Eastern Elsweyr Gate in Cyrodiil.'' '''Artifact Weapons''' are used in PvP. ===[[ON:Volendrung|Volendrung]]=== [[File:ON-item-Volendrung 02.jpg|Volendrung|thumb]] :''The legendary hammer, Volendrung, fuses Dwarven ingenuity with the seething wrath of the Daedric Prince Malacath. Its true nature and complex loyalties remain a matter of intense debate, but in the hands of a skilled warrior, its power is undeniable.'' [[ON:Volendrung|Volendrung]] is only available in Cyrodiil. Its introductory quest is [[ON:Chaos Magic|Chaos Magic]]. This artifact is replicated by an [[ON:Volendrung Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===Datamined=== [[File:ON-render-Auriel's Bow.jpg|thumb|right|Auriel's Bow]] [[ON:Sanguine's Rose|Sanguine's Rose]] and [[ON:Auriel's Bow|Auriel's Bow]] might appear in future updates. [[General:Rich Lambert|Rich Lambert]] has stated that while there are plans to add more artifacts to Cyrodiil, they are still working on polishing Volendrung's functionality before introducing newer artifacts. {{NewLine}} ==Quest Artifacts== These items can only be seen or used during a specific quest, and are always associated with solo play areas, so you can never see two players with the items at the same time. They also provide you with unique abilities, generally only useful during their associated quest. {{Incomplete}} ===The Amulet of Kings=== [[File:ON-item-Amulet of Kings.jpg|thumb|The Amulet of Kings]][[File:ON-icon-misc-Amulet of Kings.png|left]] :''An ancient artifact of Akatosh with mysterious powers.'' The [[Lore:Amulet of Kings|Amulet of Kings]] is acquired during [[Online:Shadow of Sancre Tor|Shadow of Sancre Tor]], hidden in the ruin by Sai Sahan, who was tortured for two years by Mannimarco to tell him the location. It is used as part of the Dragonfire ritual vision in [[ON:The Harborage (quest)|The Harborage]] and later in the sacrifice for [[ON:God of Schemes|God of Schemes]], with [[ON:Abnur Tharn|Abnur Tharn]] disappearing with it afterwards. He later says he hid the amulet after discovering its power was temporarily drained. {{NewLine}} ===Blade of Woe=== [[File:ON-quest-A Lesson in Silence.jpg|Blade of Woe|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Dwarven Dagger-Daedric.png|left]] The power to use the Blade of Woe is granted to members of the [[Online:Dark Brotherhood|Dark Brotherhood]], appearing out of thin air when used and disappearing afterwards. It uses the tier 3 [[Online:Daedric Style|daedric]] dagger style. {{NewLine}} ===Crown of Freydis=== [[File:ON-item-Crown of Freydis.jpg|Crown of Freydis|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-misc-Silver Crown.png|left]] :''This crown is ornate, and very cold to the touch. This close to Sovngarde, it hums gently.'' The [[Lore:Crown of Freydis|Crown of Freydis]] is {{Item Link|seen|questid=3992}} in [[ON:Songs of Sovngarde|Songs of Sovngarde]], where it is brought to [[ON:Skuldafn|Skuldafn]] and presented before the Ebonheart Pact leaders at the Great Moot to seal their alliance. {{NewLine}} ===Crown of Nenalata=== [[File:ON-item-Crown of Nenalata.jpg|Crown of Nenalata|thumb]] The [[Lore:Crown of Nenalata|Crown of Nenalata]] is on display in the [[Online:Mages Guild (Marbruk)|Marbruk Guild Vault]]. [[ON:King Laloriaran Dynar|King Laloriaran Dynar]] also wears a crown, though it is unclear what relation it has. {{NewLine}} ===Dawnbreaker=== [[File:ON-npc-Golden Knight 03.jpg|The Golden Knight|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-quest-Dawnbreaker.png|left]] :''The legendary sword of Meridia radiates with power.'' [[Lore:Dawnbreaker|Dawnbreaker]] is wielded by [[ON:Golden Knight|The Golden Knight]] and is instrumental during the Summerset main questline. The Knight allows you to use its abilities to smite enemies in various quests. It can also be acquired [[ON:Dawnbreaker|as a skill]] in the Fighters Guild skilline. This artifact will be replicated by an [[ON:Dawnbreaker Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===Ebony Blade=== [[File:ON-item-Ebony Blade.jpg|Ebony Blade|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Greatsword-Ebony Blade.png|left]] The [[Lore:Ebony Blade|Ebony Blade]] is seen during [[Online:Edge of Darkness|Edge of Darkness]] as a one handed weapon. The [[ON:Ebony Blade Style|outfit style]] is [[Skyrim:Ebony Blade|inspired]] by the Ebony Blade from [[Skyrim:Skyrim|Skyrim]]. {{NewLine}} ===The Fork of Horripilation=== [[File:ON-quest-The Lunacy of Two Moons Fork of Horripilation.jpg|thumb|The Fork in a roast steak]][[File:ON-icon-misc-Fork of Horripilation.png|left]] :''A twin-tined fork made of some kind of base iron metal. Smells lightly of roast beef.'' The [[Lore:Fork of Horripilation|Fork of Horripilation]] is an artifact of [[ON:Sheogorath|Sheogorath]]. He requests you obtain it from [[ON:Korthor|Korthor]] during [[ON:Simply Misplaced|Simply Misplaced]], who {{Item Link|drops|questid=3725}} it upon defeat. It {{Item Link|appears|questid=6888}} once again at a Ruddy Fangs camp north of [[ON:Two Moons at Tenmar Temple|Two Moons at Tenmar Temple]] during [[ON:The Lunacy of Two Moons|The Lunacy of Two Moons]]. This artifact is replicated by an [[ON:Fork of Horripilation Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===The Mace of Molag Bal=== [[File:ON-item-Mace of Molag Bal.jpg|thumb|The Mace of Molag Bal]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Mace-Mace of Molag Bal.png|left]] The [[Lore:Mace of Molag Bal|Mace of Molag Bal]] is wielded by the eponymous [[Online:Molag Bal|Daedric Prince]] during [[Online:God of Schemes|God of Schemes]], and can be seen holding it throughout the Main and Coldharbour quests. It is also replicated by an [[Online:Mace of Molag Bal Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===Mehrunes' Razor=== [[File:ON-item-Mehrunes' Razor.jpg|Mehrunes' Razor|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Sword-Mehrunes' Razor.png|left]] [[Lore:Mehrunes' Razor|Mehrunes' Razor]] wielded by [[Online:Gilraen|Gilraen]] during [[ON:Return to Ash|Return to Ash]], having become the "Razor Master". This artifact is replicated by an [[ON:Mehrunes' Razor Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===Mnemic Egg=== [[File:ON-icon-furnishing-Replica Mnemic Egg.png|left]] [[File:ON-furnishing-Replica Mnemic Egg.jpg|Mnemic Egg|thumb]] The [[Lore:Mnemic Egg|Mnemic Egg]] is seen during [[ON:Songs of Sovngarde|Songs of Sovngarde]], where it is brought to [[ON:Skuldafn|Skuldafn]] and presented before the Ebonheart Pact leaders at the Great Moot to seal their alliance. {{NewLine}} ===Muatra=== [[File:ON-item-Muatra.jpg|Muatra|thumb]] [[Lore:Muatra|Muatra]] is a unique staff wielded by [[ON:Vivec|Vivec]]. It is mentioned throughout the [[Online:Vivec's 36 Lessons|36 Lessons of Vivec]], and Vivec holds it a number of times throughout the Morrowind Main Quest. It is not directly referred to by its name, and is called VivecSpear_Staff in the files. {{NewLine}} ===Prismatic Crystal=== [[File:ON-icon-misc-Glowing Gem.png|left]] [[File:ON-misc-The Prismatic Core.jpg|thumb|right|The Prismatic Crystal]] :''This gem contains the soul of a Meridian priestess.'' The [[Lore:Artifacts P|Prismatic Crystal]] is {{Item Link|obtained|questid=2759}} from [[ON:Mzeneldt|Mzeneldt]] during [[ON:The Dangerous Past|The Dangerous Past]]. It is later forged into the Prismatic Weapon of your choice. {{NewLine}} ===Rootmender's Staff=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Rootmender's Staff.png|left]] [[File:ON-item-weapon-Rootmender's Staff.jpg|thumb|right|Rootmender's Staff]] {{Item Link|Rootmender's Staff|id=145544|quality=4|summary=1}} is granted as a quest reward for [[Online:By River and Root|By River and Root]]. {{NewLine}} ===The Skeleton Key=== [[File:ON-item-Skeleton Key.jpg|thumb|Skeleton Key connected to Sotha Sil]][[File:ON-icon-furnishing-Skeleton Key.png|left]] The [[Lore:Skeleton Key|Skeleton Key]] is an artifact associated with [[ON:Nocturnal|Nocturnal]], stated as an unbreakable lockpick, but possesses far greater powers. It was stolen by the [[ON:Blackfeather Court|Blackfeather Court]] and stored in the [[ON:Incarnatorium|Incarnatorium]], later taken back by the [[ON:Shadow of Sotha Sil|Shadow of Sotha Sil]] during [[ON:Lost in the Gloam|Lost in the Gloam]]. It is then used by Nocturnal and the Shadow in an attempt to unlock the inner workings of [[ON:Sotha Sil|Sotha Sil]]'s mind in [[ON:Where Shadows Lie|Where Shadows Lie]], with the Key being given to [[ON:Divayth Fyr|Divayth Fyr]] after Nocturnal's plot is thwarted. A [[:File:ON-furnishing-Skeleton Key Replica.jpg|replica furnishing]] can afterwards be purchased from [[ON:Razoufa|Razoufa]] {{NewLine}} ===Spellbreaker=== [[File:ON-npc-Zaan the Scalecaller 02.jpg|Spellbreaker|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-quest-Spellbreaker.png|left]] [[Lore:Spellbreaker|Spellbreaker]] is wielded by [[Online:Zaan the Scalecaller|Zaan the Scalecaller]] in Scalecaller Peak. This artifact is replicated by an [[ON:Spellbreaker Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===Staff of Magnus=== [[File:ON-item-Staff of Magnus.jpg|thumb|The Staff of Magnus in the vault, later discovered to be an illusion cast by its thief]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Staff of Magnus.png|left]] :''This is the legendary artifact that was allegedly wielded by Magnus himself. I must now return it to Queen Ayrenn for safekeeping.'' The [[Lore:Staff of Magnus|Staff of Magnus]] is an artifact associated with the god [[Lore:Magnus (god)|Magnus]]. It is initially stored in the Mages Guild vault at Marbruk during [[ON:The Staff of Magnus|The Staff of Magnus]], before it is discovered as being stolen by the [[ON:Veiled Heritance|Veiled Heritance]]. The [[ON:Shade of Naemon|Shade of Naemon]] later uses it on the Heart of Valenwood at Hectahame during [[ON:Striking at the Heart|Striking at the Heart]], and is {{Item Link|retrieved|questid=4263}} after his defeat. {{NewLine}} ===Staff of Towers=== [[File:ON-weapon-Staff of Towers.jpg|thumb|Josajeh wielding the Staff of Towers]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Staff of Towers.png|left]] The [[Lore:Staff of Towers|Staff of Towers]] is assembled during the [[ON:Psijic Order|Psijic Order]] questline. {{NewLine}} ===Staff of Worms=== [[File:ON-npc-Mannimarco.jpg|Mannimarco holding the Staff of Worms|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Mannimarco.png|left]] The [[Lore:Staff of Worms|Staff of Worms]] is a [[ON:Mannimarco Style|unique]] staff commonly seen as being held by [[ON:Mannimarco|Mannimarco]]. It is depicted as a having metallic prongs on the end with a skull inside the top. He seldom uses it, but casts a few spells with it throughout the [[ON:Main Quest|Main Quest]]. {{NewLine}} ===Sunna'rah=== [[File:ON-item-Sunna'rah.jpg|thumb|Sunna'rah]][[File:ON-icon-quest-Sunna'rah.png|left]] :''Created by Sotha Sil, this staff-like device combines clockwork technology with magicka.'' [[Lore:Sunna'rah|Sunna'rah]] is a staff created by [[ON:Sotha Sil|Sotha Sil]]. It is {{Item Link|first obtained|questid=6099}} in [[ON:Divine Intervention|Divine Intervention]] and {{Item Link|once again|questid=6113}} in [[ON:Divine Restoration|Divine Restoration]]. The staff is used by both [[ON:Chodala|Chodala]] and [[ON:Barbas|Barbas]]. {{NewLine}} ===Ul'Vor Staff=== [[File:ON-item-Ul'Vor Staff.jpg|Ul'Vor Staff|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Ul'Vor Staff.png|left]] :''An ancient relic thought to have originated in the Sea Sload kingdom of Ul'vor-Kus.'' The [[Lore:Artifacts U|Ul'Vor Staff]] was a mysterious magical Sea Sload stave stored in the Psijic Relic Vaults. It is {{Item Link|used|questid=6592}} to tap into the mind of [[ON:K'Tora|K'Tora]] during [[ON:Buried Memories|Buried Memories]] {{NewLine}} ===Veloth's Judgment=== [[File:ON-item-Veloth's-Judgement.png|Veloth's Judgment|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Dwarven Maul-Daedric.png|left]] [[Lore:Veloth's Judgement|Veloth's Judgment]] is wielded by [[ON:Magistrix Vox|Magistrix Vox]] during the [[ON:Deshaan|Deshaan]] questline and is later seen during [[ON:Songs of Sovngarde|Songs of Sovngarde]], where it is brought to [[ON:Skuldafn|Skuldafn]] and presented before the Ebonheart Pact leaders at the Great Moot to seal their alliance. {{NewLine}} ===Wabbajack=== [[File:ON-item-weapon-Wabbajack.jpg|Wabbajack|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-misc-Wabbajack.png|left]] :''A long staff with many faces adorning its tip.'' [[Lore:Wabbajack|Wabbajack]] is used by the player during [[ON:Simply Misplaced|Simply Misplaced]], and is given back to [[Online:Sheogorath|Sheogorath]] at the end of the quest. Some players managed to take it out of the intended area using a [[Online:Assistants|Banking Assistant]] upon their release, but it was quickly patched. Anyone that managed to take it out was able to keep the staff. It is a common quality level 1 healing staff that has a total of 858 damage. It fires a red beam unlike other healing staffs, and the intended targets for it to be used on are the [[Online:Temple Acolyte (Vulkhel Guard)|temple acolytes]] during the quest. When used on the acolytes, they can undergo the following transformations: *A [[ON:Bantam Guar|Bantam Guar]]. *A [[ON:Cat|cat]]. *A stone cat. *A cheese wedge. *A [[ON:Chicken|chicken]]. *A hostile [[ON:Dremora Caitiff|Dremora Caitiff]]. *A hostile [[ON:Flame Atronach|Flame Atronach]]. *A friendly Flame Atronach. *A hostile [[ON:Pig|Pig]] that vanishes after a few seconds. *A hostile [[ON:Skeletal Soldier|Skeletal Soldier]]. *A immobile Skeletal Soldier statue. *A statue. *A gourd plant. *Back to themselves. ===Wraithguard=== [[File:ON-item-Wraithguard.jpg|Wraithguard|thumb]] [[Lore:Wraithguard|Wraithguard]] is worn by [[Online:Vivec|Vivec]]. {{NewRight}} ===Unique Gear=== {{cleanup|Needs info on each}} File:ON-icon-armor-Head-Hound.png|The Hound's mask File:ON-icon-armor-Helmet-Mane.png|Crown of the Mane File:ON-icon-armor-Head-Wilderking.png|Wilderking Crown File:ON-icon-armor-Head-Barbas.png|Barbas' battle helmet {{NewLine}} ==Dropped Artifacts== Various artifacts were previously available as usable weapons during the beta, coming with their own abilities and sets. They could be obtained from various Veteran [[ON:Group Dungeons|Group Dungeon]]s, with some remnants being left in until [[ON:Update 4|Update 4]] when quite a few of them were renamed to other sets with generic items (before those sets were also removed from the game), likely having been replaced with the [[ON:Monster Helm Sets|Monster Helms]] system. The only artifact to make it past launch was Trueflame. ===Trueflame=== [[File:ON-item-weapon-Trueflame.jpg|Trueflame|thumb]][[File:ON-icon-weapon-Trueflame.png|left]] [[Lore:Trueflame|Trueflame]] was the legendary blade of [[ON:Nerevar|Nerevar]]. It is a unique one-handed sword and part of the [[ON:Arms of Infernace|Arms of Infernace]] set, dealing between 168–1335 weapon damage based on the level, and is able to deal up to 2534 flame damage. It could previously be obtained from [[ON:Fishing|fishing]] in [[ON:Stonefalls|Stonefalls]] before it was patched in [[Online:Patch/1.0.1|Patch 1.0.1]]. Those who obtained the sword before its removal were still able to keep it, but unable to trade it as it is a bound item. {{NewLine}} ===Hopesfire=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Sword-Hopesfire.png|left]] [[Lore:Hopesfire|Hopesfire]] is the legendary blade of [[ON:Almalexia|Almalexia]], though she is not seen with it equipped. It is a unique one-handed sword part of the [[ON:Arms of Infernace|Arms of Infernace]] set, dealing between 168–1335 weapon damage based on the level, and is able to deal up to 2534 flame damage. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons. {{NewLine}} ===Crusader's Mace=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Mace-Crusader's Mace.png|left]] The [[Lore:Mace of the Crusader|Crusader's Mace]] is one of the legendary relics of [[Lore:Pelinal Whitestrake|Pelinal Whitestrake]]. It is a unique one-handed mace part of the [[ON:Relics of the Rebellion|Relics of the Rebellion]] set. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons, likely [[ON:Crypt of Hearts II|Veteran Crypt of Hearts]]. Curiously, its icon is used by [[ON:Unzoned Quest Items#Molag_Bal_Relic|the Molag Bal Relic]]. {{NewLine}} ===Auriel's Shield=== [[File:ON-icon-armor-Shield-Auriel's Shield.png|left]] [[Lore:Auriel's Shield|Auriel's Shield]] is a holy relic of the god [[Lore:Auri-El|Auriel]], matching the item's appearance in [[Skyrim:Auriel's Shield|Dawnguard]]. It is a unique shield part of the [[ON:Relics of the Rebellion|Relics of the Rebellion]] set, and possessed the ability to temporarily increase one's own armor rating using magicka. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons, likely [[ON:Crypt of Hearts II|Veteran Crypt of Hearts]]. {{NewLine}} ===Auriel's Bow=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Bow-Auriel's Bow.png|left]] [[Lore:Auriel's Bow|Auriel's Bow]] is a holy relic of the god [[Lore:Auri-El|Auriel]], matching the item's appearance in [[Skyrim:Auriel's Bow|Dawnguard]]. It is a unique bow part of the [[ON:Arms of the Ancestors|Arms of the Ancestors]] set, previously obtainable from various veteran dungeons. Many skills for the artifact have appeared in the game files, suggesting it will appear as a PvP artifact. {{NewLine}} ===Staff of Indarys=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff of Indarys.png|left]] The [[Oblivion:Staff of Indarys|Staff of Indarys]] is an artifact resembling a tree branch. It is a healing staff part of the [[ON:Relics of the Physician, Ansur|Relics of the Physician, Ansur]] set, and possessed an enchantment dealing shock and magic damage and restoring magicka. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons. {{NewLine}} ===Spear of Bitter Mercy=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Spear of Bitter Mercy.png|left]] The [[Lore:Spear of Bitter Mercy|Spear of Bitter Mercy]] is a Daedric artifact. It is a unique lightning staff part of the [[ON:The Destruction Suite|Destruction Suite]] set, dealing between 168–1335 weapon damage based on the level, able to deal up to 2534 Shock Damage, as well as increase your power by 348 for 5 seconds. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons. The artifact appeared as an [[Online:Spear of Bitter Mercy Style|outfit style]]. {{NewLine}} ===Staff of St. Llothis=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Staff of St. Llothis.png|left]] The [[Lore:Crosier of St. Llothis|Staff of St. Llothis]] is an artifact of [[ON:Saint Llothis the Pious|St. Llothis]]. It is a unique flame staff part of the [[ON:The Destruction Suite|Destruction Suite]] set, enchanted to deal Unresistable and Flame damage. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons. {{NewLine}} ===Hrormir's Ice Staff=== [[File:ON-icon-weapon-Staff-Hrormir's Ice Staff.png|left]] [[Lore:Hrormir's Icestaff|Hrormir's Ice Staff]] is an artifact of Hrormir, a one-time champion of [[ON:Nocturnal|Nocturnal]]. It is a unique frost staff part of the [[ON:The Destruction Suite|Destruction Suite]] set, enchanted to deal Frost damage. It could previously be obtained from various veteran dungeons. {{NewLine}} ===Other=== The following icons depict artifacts that originated in previous Elder Scrolls games and were intended to appear, Online:Ruddy Fangs:
<noinclude>{{Mod Header|Elsweyr}}{{Trail|Factions}}[[File:ON-npc-Ruddy Fang Cutthroat.jpg|thumb|right|A member of the Ruddy Fangs]]</noinclude>
The [[Online:Ruddy Fangs|Ruddy Fangs]] are a [[ON:Khajiit|Khajiit]] bandit pride operating in [[ON:Northern Elsweyr|Northern]] and [[ON:Southern Elsweyr|Southern Elsweyr]], led by [[ON:Zayreba Sharpclaw|Zayreba Sharpclaw]]. They have the biggest presence near [[ON:The Scar|the Scar]], but are a scourge upon all of Elsweyr.<noinclude>

Their main source of income is smuggling things to and from Elsweyr, with one of their biggest products being [[Lore:Skooma|Skooma]]. They also partake in the slave trade. Those within the ranks of the Ruddy Fangs are required to throw out any morals, and the only way to get out of the business is death.

Recently, the Ruddy Fangs began preying on refugees fleeing the rage of [[ON:Dragon|dragon]]s unleashed from the [[ON:Halls of Colossus|Halls of Colossus]], prowling the roads for any opportunities to obtain more goods. While the Ruddy Fangs in Northern Elsweyr are all Khajiit, those found in Southern Elsweyr include members of other races as well. {{FMI}}

Most documents and folios require also a certain achievement to be unlocked before you are eligible to buy them.

==Folios==

Online:Antiquity Leads:
{{Trail|Items}}{{Mod Header|Greymoor}}{{TOCright|limit=2}}
'''Antiquity Leads''' are items that are used to [[ON:Scrying|Scry]] for [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]]. They can be found in a wide variety of ways and places throughout the world. You don't need to be an [[ON:Antiquarian Circle|Antiquarian]] to find them, but you do to use them. Some Leads may require you to have done other tasks before you can obtain them – exploring a zone, completing a quest, or digging up other Antiquities. 

* Leads expire 30 days after you obtain them, though you can obtain them again.
* Leads are account-wide. This means if you discover a Lead on one character, another character can scry and excavate it.
* Leads have fixed locations, such as drops from certain enemies, containers or merchants.

Lead sourcing is often related to the Antiquity it will lead to. For example, Leads to Antiquities regarding Glenumbra's history will be found in Glenumbra. For information on where to find Leads sorted by Zone, see: '''[[Online:Antiquities by Zone|Antiquities by Zone]]'''.

{{NewLine}}

==Difficulty Levels==
Leads come in various difficulties, and it determines how challenging the [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]] and [[ON:Excavation|Excavation]] mini-games are. There are five levels, but the difficulty of the Lead doesn't always accurately relate to the quality of the antiquity. For example, an '''{{ESO Quality Color|s|intermediate-difficulty}}''' Lead can uncover an '''{{ESO Quality Color|e|epic quality}}''' item.

===Simple===
'''{{ESO Quality Color|f|Simple}}''' Leads can be scried by default and consist of mainly treasures, motifs chapters and [[ON:Antique Maps|antique maps]]. Every zone has one Simple Lead given to you for free. 

===Intermediate===
'''{{ESO Quality Color|s|Intermediate}}''' Leads consist of mainly treasures, motifs chapters, cosmetics, and mount components. You need to be at least level 3 in Scrying, and have the '''[[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight II]]''' passive to scry for Antiquities of this difficulty.

===Advanced===
'''{{ESO Quality Color|e|Advanced}}''' Leads consist of mainly treasures, motifs chapters, mount components and [[ON:Antiquity Furnishings|epic-quality furnishings]]. You need to be at least level 5 in Scrying, and have the '''[[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight III]]''' passive to scry for Antiquities of this difficulty.

===Master===
'''{{ESO Quality Color|l|Master}}''' Leads consist of mainly Mythic item and mount components, and some [[ON:Antiquity Furnishings|legendary-quality furnishings]]. You need to be at least level 7 in Scrying, and have the '''[[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]]''' passive to scry for Antiquities of this difficulty.

===Ultimate===
'''{{ESO Quality Color|l|Ultimate}}''' Leads consists mostly of a selected range of [[ON:Antiquity Furnishings|legendary-quality furnishings]]. You need to be at least level 10 in Scrying, and have the '''[[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight V]]''' passive to scry for Antiquities of this difficulty. 

Ultimate Leads appear in the same shade of gold as Master Leads, making it difficult to distinguish between the two. The following is a list of all Ultimate Leads:

==Mythic Items==
[[ON:Mythic Items|Mythic Items]] are broken up into 5 fragments, each requiring a Master difficulty Lead to find. These Leads may require owning additional DLCs or Chapters to discover or excavate, in addition to the piece of content the Mythic item was released alongside. 

For example, the [[ON:Ring of the Pale Order|Ring of the Pale Order]] was released with the Markarth DLC, but it also requires access to the Orsinium DLC in order to find all fragment Leads. In addition, the Greymoor chapter is ''also'' required to Scry these Leads via the [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]] skill line. The table below shows the DLCs required to complete a particular Mythic item. 

Alongside having access to the appropriate content, you are required to be at least level 7 in [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]], and have the [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight IV]] passive in order to scry Master difficulty leads. The dig site for fragments are usually found in the same zone as where the Lead drops, save for a few cases where it must be excavated in a different zone.

The '''Aspect of Alkosh'''{{ref|name=ESO|Name according to model data.}} is a giant golden [[ON:Dragon|dragon]] seen from afar in the [[ON:Spilled Sand|Spilled Sand]] illusion created by the Mask of Alkosh during [[Online:The Dragonguard|The Dragonguard]]. It is incredibly long and spans most of the realm. Its eyes are always closed, slumbering in the sands.

It is not possible to reach it without bypassing the teleportation effect that occurs after getting too far out.

They are among his highest ranking commanders, and serve as officers in his [[ON:Daedra|Daedric]] legion. Their leader, [[ON:Valkynaz Nokvroz|Valkynaz Nokvoz]], currently rules the citadel of [[ON:Ardent Hope|Ardent Hope]].

{{Mod Header|Gold Road}}{{Trail|Lucent Citadel|nocat=1}}[[Category:Online-Items]][[File:ON-mapicon-Arcane Knot (whole).png|left]][[File:ON-item-Arcane Knot.jpg|thumb|right|Arcane Knot]] The '''Arcane Knot''' is a 'capture-the-flag' objective in the [[Online:Lucent Citadel|Lucent Citadel]]. It is a unique mechanic of the [[Online:Trials|trial]]. {{FMI}} {{NewLeft}} ===Recovering the Arcane Knot=== The Arcane Knot is located in the Catalyst Nook, the final section of Lucent Citadel. It needs to be picked up by a player and returned to the entrance of the trial, where it can safely be deposited into a device called the '''null arca'''. If the player dies, another member of the group will need to claim the Knot. To complete the trial, players must carry the Arcane Knot from the Catalyst Nook to the start of the Faceted Gallery (entrance). Along the path, several Crystal Shards, as seen throughout the trial, must be destroyed to allow progress through crystal barriers. These barriers blocked your group on the approach, but for the return journey it will make the path back a lot shorter. === Arcane Fracture and Temporal Splinters === [[File:ON-mapicon-Arcane Knot (broken).png|left]] A player can use the Interact Key (default bound key E) to pick up the Arcane Knot. It can be held by the player for 1 minute (45 seconds in Hard Mode) before they are forced to drop it. During this time, the knot damages the player with '''Temporal Splinters''', which deals ramping-up direct [[ON:Oblivion Damage|oblivion damage]]. The knot 'explodes' when the timer expires and other players should not be caught within the large AoE blast radius dealing high [[ON:Magic Damage|magic damage]] ('''Arcane Fracture'''). When the Arcane Knot is not held by a player, it deals ramping direct magic damage to all players until it is picked up or the group wipes ('''Arcane Swarm'''). Once dropped, a debuff is applied to the player for 8 minutes. Any attempt to pick up the knot again within this time will result in instant death. Thus, players must take turns picking up and carrying the knot. {{ESO Achievements List |Tight Grip |Interplanar Cohesion }} === Arcane Encumbrance === [[File:ON-mapicon-Arcane Knot (carry).png|left]] While holding the Arcane Knot, and while other players are within the Arcane Knot dome, players have slowed movement speed depending on how many players are within the dome of the knot. The fewer the players, the slower the movement speed. It is recommended to keep up with the carrier to ensure they can move with the knot.
Each time the knot timer expires and a new carrier is required, a [[Online:Crystal Atronach|Crystal Atronach]] will spawn ('''Summon Atronach'''). {{NewLine}} ==Gallery== File:ON-item-Arcane Knot 02.jpg|A player running with the Arcane Knot File:ON-item-Arcane Knot (Null Arca).jpg|The Arcane Knot contained in the null arca File:ON-render-Lucent Citadel 03.jpg|[[Online:Renders/Gold Road|Pre-release render]]

Online:Woodworking Materials:
{{Trail|Items}} There are four types of materials involved in [[ON:Woodworking|Woodworking]]: Wood, Sanded Wood, Resins, and Gems. Wood is the raw material that can be found in the world by harvesting fallen logs. By themselves they cannot be used, but they may be refined into Sanded Wood at any woodworking station. Unlocking the "Plentiful Harvest" and "Master Gatherer" perks in the Craft [[Online:Champion#Craft|Champion]] tree will also provide bonuses when harvesting. There is a small chance of producing resins when refining raw materials. The logs you find are determined by your character's level and your [[Online:Woodworking (skill)|Woodworking]] level—if you are level 40 with a Woodworking level of 2, you will find both Rough Oak and Rough Hickory out in the world. Sanded Wood is used to make [[ON:Shields|shields]] as well as all bows and staves. Resins can be used to improve existing shields or weapons. Resins can be obtained by deconstructing existing armor sets. Rough wood and resins can both be acquired through [[ON:Lumberjack Hireling|Lumberjack Hireling]] mails. Sanded wood and resins can be obtained as rewards for completing [[Online:Woodworker Writ|Woodworker Writs]]. Gems are used to craft weapons or armor with traits, provided that trait has been researched on that piece. {{trail|Items}}[[File:ON-item-Soul Gems.jpg|thumb|right|A pile of soul gems]]
'''Soul Gems''' have two uses in ''[[Online:Online|Elder Scrolls Online]]''. They may be used to recharge [[Online:Enchanting|enchanted]] [[Online:weapons|weapons]], and they may also be used to revive either yourself or other players. Both empty and filled soul gems can be received as rewards from [[ON:Chest|chest]]s, in containers from completing quests, and from picking up [[#Samples|physical samples]] throughout the world (usually around [[Online:Mystics|Mystics]]). {{Crown Link|Crown Soul Gem Pack|Crown Soul Gem}}s{{Crown Store}} can be earned from certain [[ON:Golden Pursuits|Golden Pursuits]] or purchased from the [[ON:Crown Store|Crown Store]] and used as an alternative.

==Gameplay==
[[File:ON-render-Resurrection.jpg|thumb|right|Player being resurrected]]
Soul gems may be found in loot or purchased from vendors, and they may be either empty or full. If a soul gem is empty, you will need to fill it before it can be used. You can do this by casting the [[Online:Soul Trap|Soul Trap]] skill (from the [[Online:Soul Magic|Soul Magic]] skill line) on an enemy before killing it. You must kill the enemy before the soul trap effect, apparent as a white glow around the target, wears off. There are also certain skills and sets that allow you to capture souls without the use of Soul Trap.

To recharge a weapon, select it in the Inventory menu, and the "Recharge" option will appear. Press the key/button associated with it ({{pc22}} you may also right-click and select "Recharge" from the drop-down menu). Select the soul gem and click "Recharge", and you will regain charge on the weapon.

Soul gems are also used to revive dead players. If you have a filled soul gem in your inventory, you'll be given the option when you die of reviving with your own soul gem or reviving at the nearest [[Online:Wayshrines|wayshrine]]. Reviving yourself with a soul gem will grant you an ethereal form for a short time that is unable to attack or be attacked in any way. This can allow you to get out of danger or regroup in a safe spot before the ghostly effect wears off. 

In some situations you will not be allowed to revive yourself on the spot, even if you have filled soul gems. This is the case in PvP, during dungeon boss fights and when the group is in combat in a trial. However, other players may still attempt to revive you. The other player must hold down the use button when they are near your corpse (indicated by a plus sign). This only works if they have a filled soul gem. If you accept, you will be revived on the spot and their soul gem will be consumed. Do note that accepting a revive this way will skip the ghostly phase leaving you vulnerable at once. Ensure it is safe to revive before pressing accept.

There is an option to toggle Crown Soul Gems as the default for resurrection instead.

==Samples==
[[File:ON-item-Soul Gems 02.jpg|thumb|right|Soul gems at a market stall]]
There are a number of locations where Soul Gem samples can spawn. In settlements they are most often found on counters, tables, and shelves near [[Online:Mystics|Mystics]]; many of them are marked as owned, so picking them up will mark them as stolen. They vary in appearance from looking like anything between petty and grand soul gems, as their appearance was once a factor in the level of the gem until Update 12, but now all of them are considered standard soul gems regardless of appearance. They will also respawn.

Online:Sets:
{{Trail|Items}}
'''Sets''' are groups of items that provide powerful extra bonuses when matched pieces are equipped, up to a maximum of five pieces. You can receive benefits from more than one set (e.g. getting the 2-item bonuses from four different sets). Regardless of equipment type, you will have twelve equipment slots open to you. Most sets are available in all armor slots and in most traits.

Sets are divided into two main types: bind-on-equip and bind-on-pickup. Bind-on-equip items are permanently bound to your account only when you equip them. Bind-on-pickup set items can only be traded for two hours after the item is received and only with other group members within the instance when you received it; after which the item is permanently bound to your account.

Once an item is added to your [[ON:Collections#Set Items|set collection]], it can be reconstructed with [[ON:Transmute Crystals|transmute crystals]].

==Arena Sets==
[[ON:Arena Sets|Arena Sets]] are five-piece sets that can be found from group and solo [[ON:Arenas|Arenas]]. Reward chests give these set items after every round.

==Craftable Sets==
[[ON:Craftable Sets|Craftable Sets]] can be created at various locations. To craft set items, you must find one of their special [[ON:Crafting Sites|crafting sites]]. For most sets, there is one crafting site in each [[ON:Alliances|Alliance]]'s territory. Other sets become available upon completion of certain quest lines, including the [[ON:Fighters Guild|Fighters Guild]], and the [[ON:Mages Guild|Mages Guild]]. Some crafting sites are found in DLC zones, and can only be accessed if you own the DLC. Nevertheless, it is possible to wear gear from those sets even if you do not own the DLC, if someone else crafts the gear for you. All crafted gear is bind-on-equip.

Additionally, to craft a set item, you must have [[ON:Traits#Research|researched]] a number of [[ON:Traits|traits]] for that specific item type. The more complicated sets require more traits to be known, and hence more research.

Before the Summerset Chapter, jewelry crafting was not available; crafted set items could only be made for the seven equipment and two weapon slots. Players who purchased the Summerset Chapter expansion can now make rings and necklaces for any crafted set, provided the trait requirements have been met for that set. Players who have not purchased the expansion do not have access at this time, but can purchase crafted jewelry from guild traders or have another make it for them.

==Dungeon Sets==
[[ON:Dungeon Sets|Dungeon Sets]] can be found from normal and veteran [[ON:Group Dungeons|Group Dungeons]]. Bosses and minibosses will always drop pieces from these sets in specific slots. Dungeon sets are all bind-on-pickup, but you can trade them with your dungeon group for a while after picking up.

==Monster Helm Sets==
[[ON:Monster Helm Sets|Monster Helm Sets]] are a subset of dropped sets of armor. There are only two items available in a Monster Set: the head and the shoulders. The head pieces drop from the final boss of the associated Veteran mode group dungeon, and like the Dungeon Sets listed above, can be traded with your dungeon group for a short while before it binds permanently to your account. Shoulder pieces are acquired from coffers purchased with keys from the Undaunted Daily Pledge Givers and are bind-on-pickup.

==Mythic Items==
[[ON:Mythic Items|Mythic Items]] are special one-piece sets that grant powerful bonuses. Only one mythic item can be worn at a time. They can only be obtained through the [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] system.

==Overland Sets==
[[ON:Overland Sets|Overland Sets]] are dropped by monsters within the starter zones, the fifteen main Alliance zones as well as [[ON:Coldharbour|Coldharbour]]. Each set has a specific zone that it drops from. Set items can be found from  [[ON:World Bosses|World Bosses]], delve monsters, public dungeon monsters, dolmens (or other world events) and treasure chests found within the zone. Quests in zones will also reward set items from their respective zone sets.

==PVP Sets==
[[ON:PVP Sets|PVP Sets]] can be purchased using [[ON:Alliance Points|Alliance Points]] or [[ON:Tel Var Stones|Tel Var stones]]. Vendors will sell boxes that contain a random piece of each set.

==Trial Sets==
[[ON:Trial Sets|Trial Sets]] are available from any of the [[ON:Trials|Trials]] in the game. Bosses in Trials will drop pieces of these sets. Trial sets are bind-on-pickup.

==Jewelry Sets==
[[ON:Jewelry Sets|Jewelry Sets]] are available from [[ON:Trophy Vaults|Trophy Vaults]], PvP vendors, reward mail, and first dungeons. They do not include armor pieces, but a subset of weapons, shield and jewelry. Some Jewelry sets items are bind-on-equip, some are bind-on-pickup.

==Weapon Sets==
[[ON:Weapon Sets|Weapon Sets]] are available from Arenas and Trials. They do not include armor pieces, but a subset of weapons, shield and jewelry. Weapon sets items are bind-on-pickup.

==Class Sets==
[[ON:Class Sets|Class Sets]] are available from [[ON:Infinite Archive|Infinite Archive]]. They include all armor pieces, weapons, shield and jewelry. Class sets items are bind-on-pickup.

Was replaced with [[ON:Decisive|Decisive]]. ==Research== In order to construct an item with a specific trait, it has to first be researched. This can be done at any crafting station: * Light and medium armor at Clothing stations * Bows, staves and shields at Woodworking stations * Heavy armor and metal weapons at Blacksmithing stations * Necklaces and rings at Jewelry Crafting stations Researching a trait will unlock it only for that particular type of item - e.g. researching the ''Reinforced'' trait on [[ON:Pauldrons|pauldrons]] will only allow you to construct reinforced heavy armor shoulders, but not any other heavy armor items like [[ON:Cuirasses|cuirass]] or [[ON:Sabatons|sabatons]], or any other shoulder slot items like [[ON:Epaulets|epaulets]] or [[ON:Arm Cops|arm cops]]. The only exceptions are [[ON:Robes|robes and jerkins]], which are simply two different styles of light armor chest items. Researching is performed on a per-character basis, i.e., researching a trait on one character does not unlock that trait on any other character on that account. Constructing [[ON:Craftable Sets|Craftable Sets]] requires you to have a certain number of traits researched. To start the research process, you need to have an item with the desired trait in your inventory or bank. Both found items and items crafted by other players work. Researching a trait will destroy the item. By default you can only research a single trait at a time per crafting skill, though each crafting skill line has an ability to raise this limit and increase the research speed: * {{icon|skill|Clothing-Stitching|18}} '''[[ON:Stitching|Stitching]]''' for [[ON:Clothing|Clothing]] * {{icon|skill|Woodworking-Carpentry|18}} '''[[ON:Carpentry|Carpentry]]''' for [[ON:Woodworking|Woodworking]] * {{icon|skill|Blacksmithing-Metallurgy|18}} '''[[ON:Metallurgy|Metallurgy]]''' for [[ON:Blacksmithing|Blacksmithing]] * {{icon|skill|Jewelry Crafting-Lapidary Research|18}} '''[[ON:Lapidary Research|Lapidary Research]]''' for [[ON:Jewelry Crafting|Jewelry Crafting]] These abilities can increase the research speed by up to 25%, and raise the limit of concurrent research tasks to 3 (with the exception of Lapidary Research, which does not add additional research slots). Note that even with an increased research limit, you still cannot research multiple traits on a single item type at the same time. The highest ability rank limits the research time to 10 days, which is only relevant to the 9th trait on an item, as the others would be below this limit already. Being an [[ON:ESO Plus|ESO Plus]] Subscriber further reduces research time by 10%, stacking multiplicatively with the above abilities. The base research time for a trait is 2 hours real time. Each further trait you research for an item type doubles this time - 4 hours for the second trait, 8 hours for the third trait, and so forth. Research time continues to count down while you are not playing the character that is researching (e.g. playing another character or offline). Online:Treasures:
{{Trail|Items}} {{Center|{{ESO Contraband}}}}[[File:ON-icon-Stolen.png|thumb|48px|Stolen item icon]] '''Treasure''', also known as '''Contraband''' items, are items that exist only to be sold in exchange for gold, as well as to add some flavor to the game. They are bound to a player's account and so cannot be traded to other players. There are many different types of treasure items, meaning that a character collecting treasures can have their inventory fill up fast. Treasures not being kept for a personal collection should therefore be sold periodically. This page does not encompass [[Online:Crafting Motifs|Crafting Motifs]], [[Online:Style Materials|style materials]], [[Online:Provisioning|provisioning ingredients]] or furnishings which can be stolen; only the items whose only purpose is to be sold to a fence (or vendor, depending on the item's source) for gold. Treasures are most commonly found by stealing: searching in [[Online:Justice|owned]] containers, pickpocketing, or looting innocent citizens you have killed. These are marked as stolen, and can be sold or laundered at [[Online:Fences|fences]]. Once laundered, the treasure can be sold to any other [[Online:Vendors|vendor]]. Treasures can also be found from other sources such as loot from [[Online:Dragons|dragons]] and [[ON:Harrowstorms|harrowstorms]], the daily rewards chest in the [[Online:Dragonguard Sanctum|Dragonguard Sanctum]], and from various [[Online:Events|event]] drops (e.g. [[ON:Plunder Skull|Plunder Skull]]s). Treasures found this way are not marked as stolen, and so can immediately be sold to a vendor or placed in the [[Online:Banks|bank]]. A treasure's sell value depends on its quality, shown in the table below. Items of higher quality are less common to find. '''Copper''' seams can be found near cliffs and mountains at [[ON:Engraver|Engraver]] level 2 or at character level 26-49.  They can be harvested for three to four samples of the raw material, {{Item Link|Copper Dust|id=135139}}. Once ten samples of dust are collected, they can be refined into seven to ten {{Item Link|Copper Ounces|id=135140}}. Copper Jewelry is [[Online:Jewelry Crafting|crafted]] from the refined copper ounces at any of the [[Online:Crafting Stations|jewelry crafting stations]].

'''Treasure Chests''' are large locked containers that can be found across Tamriel. Treasure chests [[Online:Nodes|spawn in fixed locations]] in the world. Each time they spawn, they have a random difficulty of lock—ranging from Simple to Master. They typically contain a variety of valuable items and gold.  Most chests have the same generic look, as seen in the image on the right.  Treasure chests found in [[ON:Group Dungeons|Group Dungeons]] often look different.

==Unlocking==
Unlocking a chest requires at least one lockpick, which themselves can be acquired from the world or bought from General Goods Merchants. Interacting with a chest will open up a [[ON:lockpicking|lockpicking]] mini-game where the pins must be aligned in order to open the lock. Alternatively, you can try to force the lock open. The chances of forcing a lock depends on its difficulty, but this chance can be improved by adding points to the Locksmith skill in the [[ON:Legerdemain|Legerdemain]] skill tree.

Successfully unlocking a chest grants you a small amount of leveled experience, as well as Legerdemain experience. If all the loot is taken, the chest disappears for a short time and eventually respawns.

==Skills and Perks==
There are various passive skills related to treasure chests:

* [[Online:Locksmith|Locksmith]] in the [[ON:Legerdemain|Legerdemain]] skill line — Improves the chances of forcing a lock (10% / 25% / 45% / 70%)
* [[Online:Keen Eye: Treasure Chests|Keen Eye: Treasure Chests]] in the [[ON:Excavation|Excavation]] skill line — Treasure Chests emit a glow when you are close, making them easier to see.
* [[ON:Fortune's Favor|Fortune's Favor]] in the green Craft tree ([[ON:Champion|Champion]] System) — Increases the amount of gold you find in treasure chests and safeboxes by 10% per stage.
* [[Online:Treasure Hunter (champion)|Treasure Hunter]] in the green Craft tree (Champion System) — Increases the quality of items you find in treasure chests.

==Achievements==
There are four [[ON:Achievements|Achievements]] related to Treasure Chests.
{{ESO Achievements List|multi=
{{EAL/Group
  |Treasure Chest Spotter
  |Treasure Chest Seeker
  |Treasure Chest Stalker
  |Treasure Chest Hunter}}
}}

==Notes==
* You must loot the entire contents of a chest in order to get credit for the above achievements.  Picking out the stuff you want and leaving behind the junk will not count.
* Looting the contents (again, all them) of a treasure chest will earn you {{ESO Rapport|+3|10}}/{{ESO Rapport|+1|1}} Rapport with [[ON:Mirri Elendis|Mirri Elendis]] is she is your active companion.  (The 10 points can occur once per hour, but you get 1 point for each chest after that, with no cooldown.)
* Some chests are already unlocked when you find them - notably those found by following [[ON:Treasure Maps|Treasure Maps]] or found at the end of incursion type events such as [[ON:Dark Anchors|Dark Anchors]] or in boss/side puzzle stages in the [[ON:Infinite Archive|Infinite Archive]].  These can contain the same types of items, as well as some exclusive to their specific types.  They don't give experience or Legerdemain skill, but they do count as Treasure Chests for the purposes of achievements, and for Mirri's Rapport.

of Shadows}} |} ==Kari's Hit List== Kari's Hit List is an unmarked [[ON:Museums|museum quest]] which asks the player to venture out into the world and steal a number of legendary treasures. Stolen items are put on display in the [[Online:Thieves Den|Thieves Den]]. Completing this quest awards you the [[Online:A Cutpurse Above|A Cutpurse Above]] achievement, a [[Online:Titles|Title]] and a [[Online:Mementos/DLC|Memento]]. [[Online:Kari's Hit List|Kari's Hit List]] can be found on a table in the library of Thieves Den. The library is the upper area behind the statue. The book gives a clue to the location of each item and the zone where it can be found. The items that you are looking for are unique Treasures and are listed as a Relic treasure type. They will stand out from other treasure items, as the title is in gold. These items cannot be laundered, and if you are caught by the guard and turn over stolen goods, these items will be taken from your inventory and replaced at the original location. Note that items may not be visible at the specified location if another player has recently stolen the item. {{huh|What is the respawn time?}} Once stolen, bring the items to the Thieves Den library. Near the bookcases are two table style display cases. A little searching around to find the correct location to leave each item will be necessary as quest markers are not provided. Some items just get left on the floor at specific locations. [[Online:Kari|Kari]] is sitting on a couch in the Thieves Den and can be talked to in order to learn her story. {{Trail|Factions}}{{About|the faction|the title|Truly Undaunted}}[[File:ON-banner-Undaunted.png|right|300px|]] The [[Online:Undaunted|Undaunted]] are a faction of dungeon-delving adventurers who set the scene for each of the [[Online:Group Dungeons|Group Dungeons]] and [[Online:Trials|Trials]] that can be found in [[ON:Tamriel|Tamriel]]. The locations of each of the base-game dungeons can be discovered by talking to Undaunted members within the tavern in the main city of each zone, while DLC dungeons become accessible upon unlocking the related DLC. All of the abilities give the opportunity to activate a [[Online:synergy|synergy]]. A player must be at least level 10 to join the Undaunted with the "[[ON:One of the Undaunted|One of the Undaunted]]" quest. It is possible to complete up to three pledges per character per day, a different one offered by the [[Online:Pledge Masters|three Pledge Masters]] at the Undaunted enclave. ==Daily Dungeons== The Undaunted also offer rewards for completing random dungeons through the [[Online:Grouping Tools|dungeon finder]]. Unlike pledges, there are no objectives to complete and no quest is given. The rewards and experience are automatically sent to you the moment the final boss of the dungeon dies. Completing the Daily event will grant Premium Undaunted Exploration Supplies. This event has a 20 hour cooldown per character, which means that any subsequent completion with the same character before the time is up will grant Undaunted Exploration Supplies. ==How to Excavate==
[[File:ON-activity-Antiquarian Eye.jpg|Antiquarian Eye at a dig site, pointing to the left|thumb|right]][[File:ON-skill-Keen_Eye_Dig_Sites.jpg|thumb|right|Keen Eye: Dig Sites]]
</noinclude>Once the [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]] puzzle is solved, players can travel to the marked location and perform an Excavation (which can still be done even if the Greymoor chapter is no longer accessible due to an expired ESO Plus account). These areas appear on the map outlined in cyan. Once at the location, you will need to find the place where the antiquity is thought to be buried. You can use the Antiquarian Eye found in the Tools section of your Collections (which may also be quick-slotted for ease of access) to create a comet-shaped orb of light which will show the direction of the excavation site by following where the thinner tail end of the light is pointing.

The excavation site will appear as a mound of dirt with golden motes of light coming from it. The Excavation passive skill [[ON:Keen Eye: Dig Sites|Keen Eye: Dig Sites]] makes the mounds visible from some distance away, adding cyan wisps of light and a low droning noise as you approach.

Once you have found the dig site you can start excavating, which begins another mini-game where you must excavate the treasure from a 10 x 10 square of dirt. You will have a selection of tools to help you find the antiquity and a limited number of turns for a digging attempt.<noinclude>

===Fissures===
On [[ON:Excavation#Advanced|Advanced]] and higher difficulties, the game adds fissures to the grid. These are small plumes of smoke that take up a single tile. If they are disturbed by digging directly above them they will explode and damage the antiquity, regardless of their proximity to it. The red bar at the top of your screen illustrates how many hits the antiquity can sustain. If the number in that bar drops to zero while excavating, you fail the excavation and will have to find another one within the same general area. Antiquities can also be get damaged if they are struck by digging with the heavier tools.  Note that no part of the antiquity can ever be directly below a fissure, so this can be a useful clue in determining where it might be located.

===Time===
The number of turns you have to excavate the antiquity is represented by a bronze bar at the top of the screen. It's displayed as an amount of time, but in practice, it actually represents the number of actions you can perform. Using various tools during excavation uses up "time" and depletes this bar. 

The default amount of "time" you start with is 12h 0mins, which translates to 40 actions or turns. The difficulty of the excavation doesn't change this value. The number of turns you have can be increased with the [[ON:Excavator's Reserves|Excavator's Reserves]] passive. At rank I, it increases to 45 turns and at rank II it increases to 50 turns.

Once the puzzle has been solved, the antiquity is revealed. You can continue to search for bonus items for the remaining turns you have left. These bonus items include minor loot, style materials or gold.  Notably, this is the only way to acquire {{Item Link|id=166045|Indeko}} [[ON:Runestones#Essence_Runes|runes]] for [[ON:Enchanting|Enchanting]] (other than trading with other players). The difficulty of the Lead determines how much bonus loot can be found before the mini-game ends. Green allows 1 piece of bonus loot, Blue allows 2, and so on.

==Tools==
The following tools can become available during an excavation:

===Augur===
[[File:ON-activity-Excavation Interface 03.PNG|An illustration of the different colors and their respective range|thumb|right]]
Activating the {{Item Link|collectid=8006|Antiquarian's Eye}} allows you to use the [[ON:Augur|Augur]] skill. With this, you can click on a square which will light up with a color to show how close you are to any part the antiquity (which takes up between 4 and 8 squares depending on difficulty):

* Red — A faint red outline with no glow. All of the antiquity is 5 or more squares away from the selected square.
* Orange — An orange outline with a slight glow. Part of the antiquity is within 3-4 squares away from the selected square, but not closer.
* Yellow — A yellow outline with a strong glow. Part of the antiquity is within 1-2 squares away from the selected square, but not directly underneath.
* Green — A bright green outline with a pulsating, strong glow. Part of the antiquity is directly beneath the selected square.

The number of uses you get with Eye varies by Lead difficulty as [[ON:Excavation#Difficulty Levels|detailed below]]. On higher difficulty Leads, if the dirt layer is too high the Eye will not be able to get a reading of the antiquity's location. You must first remove layers of soil to use the Augur. Alternatively, you can detect antiquities from lower layers by unlocking rank II in the Augur passive.

===Hand Brush===
{{#section:Online:Hand Brush|description}}
[[File:ON-activity-Excavation Interface 04.PNG|The squares in blue illustrate the channel of dirt that will be destroyed by a chain reaction|thumb|right]]
===Trowel===
The [[ON:Trowel|Trowel]] is unlocked at level 2, and is used to remove three layers of soil from a single 1 x 1 square. To use it requires a minimum of two charges of intuition from the Hand Brush. It may damage the antiquity if you dig too far down. Using the trowel does not deplete the "time" bar at the top of the screen.

At rank II, it can be used to safely detonate fissures and trigger soil and rock-clearing chain reactions, provided the bottom layer of dirt is reached. A chain reaction is when all the dirt between two fissures is destroyed when one of the fissures is struck with a trowel. This can only occur if all the dirt between both fissures is at the same level. Chain reactions can extend to more than two fissure, meaning that with some careful planning a large multi-fissure chain reaction can be detonated.

===Heavy Shovel===
The [[ON:Heavy Shovel|Heavy Shovel]] is unlocked at level 4 and is used to remove a single layer of dirt from a 3 x 3 square - but can only remove layers if the depth is equal to the square that was selected. To use it requires a minimum of two charges of intuition from the Hand Brush. Rank II in the Heavy Shovel passive gives you a chance to consume no intuition when it is used.

==Difficulty Levels==
===Trivial===
There is only one {{FC|grey|Trivial}} level excavation, encountered during the tutorial quest in [[ON:Solitude|Solitude]].  Dirt is only 1-2 layers deep and you get 9 charges of the Augur.  The antiquity takes up a 2 x 3 rectangle and you can excavate one piece of bonus loot.  There is no chance of damaging the antiquity as you do not have the skills that could do this yet. 

===Simple and Intermediate===
Excavations for {{ESO Quality Color|f|Simple}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|Intermediate}} Leads are relatively straightforward. Dirt can be as high as 3 layers in {{ESO Quality Color|f|Simple}} or 4 layers in {{ESO Quality Color|s|Intermediate}} and you get 8 charges of the Augur. The Rank I Augur can penetrate all levels of dirt to pin-point the treasure. 

The antiquity usually takes up a 2 x 3 rectangle, 3 x 3 square, or a total of 5 squares in the shape of a burlap sack, and only one or two pieces of bonus loot can be excavated before the excavation ends. If the antiquity is damaged 6 times it will break.

===Advanced===
Excavations for {{ESO Quality Color|e|Advanced}} Leads introduce up to 6 fissures that appear randomly across the grid, that can detonate and damage the antiquity. Dirt can be as high as 6 layers and you get 7 charges of the Augur. The Rank I Augur cannot penetrate the lowest levels of dirt, meaning at least one layer needs to be cleared before it can be used.

The antiquity usually takes up a  2 x 3 or a 2 x 4 rectangle, and three pieces of bonus loot can be excavated before the excavation ends. If the antiquity is damaged 4 times it will break.

===Master===
[[File:ON-activity-Excavation Interface 02.png|Excavation of a Master difficulty item|thumb|right]]
Excavations for {{ESO Quality Color|l|Master}} Leads are expectedly more difficult and are usually reserved for [[ON:Mythic Items|Mythic Item]] fragments and some legendary [[ON:Antiquity Furnishings|Antiquity Furnishings]]. There are usually 8 fissures, dirt can be as high as 8 layers and you get 6 charges of the Augur. Even Rank II Augur cannot penetrate the lowest levels of dirt, meaning at least two layers needs to be cleared in some areas before it can be used.

The antiquity is usually aligned in a diagonal fashion, and takes up a total of 8 squares. Four pieces of bonus loot can be excavated before the excavation ends. If the antiquity is damaged 2 times it will break.

===Ultimate===
Excavations for {{ESO Quality Color|l|Ultimate}} Leads are the hardest difficulty and are usually reserved for a selected range of [[ON:Antiquity Furnishings|legendary-quality furnishings]]. Fissures are more frequent and have a blast radius of 1 square surrounding them, meaning unintended chain reactions are possible.

Dirt can be as high as 9 layers and you get 5 charges of the Augur. Even Rank II Augur cannot penetrate the lowest levels of dirt, meaning at least three layers needs to be cleared in some parts before it can be used. If the antiquity is damaged 2 times it will break.

==Notes==
* You must have 5 free slots in your inventory else the game will not let you begin excavation.
* Once you achieve level 10 in the Scrying and Excavation skill line, {{ESO Quality Color|f|Simple}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|Intermediate}} antiquities will be the same difficulty as {{ESO Quality Color|e|Advanced}} antiquities to excavate.

==How to Scry==
===Collecting Leads===
[[File:ON-misc-Antiquities UI.jpg|thumb|The Quest Journal's [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]] tab]]
So long as the player is in an open world location, and not an instanced area such as a [[ON:Dungeons|Dungeon]], [[ON:Outlaws Refuges|Outlaws Refuge]], or the [[ON:Blackreach: Greymoor Caverns|Greymoor Caverns]], they can Scry a small selection of infinitely-cycling [[ON:Antiquities|Antiquities]]. Alternatively, while adventuring through the world, they may collect [[ON:Antiquity Leads|Leads]]. Note that collecting leads is indiscriminate of owned DLC, so you may get a lead for something you can't even scry. Indeed, you can collect leads even if you don't own the Greymoor Chapter and hence cannot access scrying.

Once you're within a non-instanced area, open the Antiquities tab in your Quest Journal. Under the "Scryable" header, you will see the tabs Current Zone (which is the default) and All Active Leads. Current Zone gives you a visual of what leads you can scry and excavate in the zone you're in, so long as you've found the lead once before. Although you can only scry Antiquities in your zone, All Active Leads shows you all active leads, including those that have been scried and are ready for excavation.

The other headers are of the major content zones: through them, you can see how many Antiquities are located in the zone, which Antiquities you have already found Leads for, and the number of codex entries each has so far. As a general rule of thumb, each Zone has one {{ESO Quality Color|f|'''Simple'''}}, {{ESO Quality Color|s|'''Intermediate'''}}, and {{ESO Quality Color|e|'''Advanced'''}} [[ON:Treasures|Treasure]], the latter of which is only obtainable once; they will appear once you have a sufficient [[ON:Antiquarian Insight|Antiquarian Insight]] Rank and, for all but the former, after you [[ON:Excavation|Excavate]] an Antiquity of a lower quality.

Use the action button on the available lead in your zone, and it will bring you into the minigame.
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface Success.jpg|thumb|left|A successful {{ESO Quality Color|e|'''Advanced'''}}-Level Scry, with all six Foci claimed]]

===The Scrying Minigame===
The minigame interface is contained within the {{Item Link|collectid=8006|Antiquarian's Eye}} you were provided: a hexagonal grid with many shape-bearing facets and six empty, spaced-out facets— known as Foci— positioned near the Eye's edge. At the very bottom of the Eye is the crystalline [[ON:Scry|Scry]] needle: starting from (or around) it, you need to click facets and expand your area of control to the Foci. You need to claim at least one of these Foci to succeed, which will turn into a white, glowing sphere when you connect a contiguous facet to your area of control.
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Facet Variation.jpg|thumb|right|The 8 different facet variations]]
Not all the facets share the same appearance, however: they vary in appearance, and can have 5 to 8 different variations depending on your Lead's difficulty level. If you click a facet that is near another of the same type, it will claim it as well— the same goes with any other contiguous facets. Some of your Scrying skills may either bypass this rule, like [[ON:Farsight (skill)|Farsight]], be impacted by it, like [[ON:Dilation|Dilation]], or contribute to it, like [[ON:Coalescence|Coalescence]]. Pay mind to what a skill does before using it, so you don't accidentally make your job harder.

Your Eye has a limited number of turns before it will automatically succeed (or fail, if you didn't claim enough Foci). It also has a limited number of {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charges, which control the use of scrying skills; once you use a skill, you will need to collect two unclaimed Foci to recharge it fully. The limits of both may be raised by [[ON:Scrier's Patience|Scrier's Patience]] and [[ON:Future Focus|Future Focus]], respectively.

Note that Foci claimed during the use of a skill count: this means that you can immediately get a {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charge back if you manage to claim two in this manner. Skills that use Charges do not consume turns, meaning that you will need to balance both turns and {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charges to claim as many Foci as desired.
[[File:ON-misc-Dig Site Map.jpg|thumb|left|The map after a successful Scry, showing five potential Antiquity spots]]
===Succeeding a Scry===
Once you successfully scry an Antiquity, your map will be populated with blue-rimmed, highlighted areas, the numbers of which equal the number of unclaimed Foci plus one (as an example: you will have four areas to explore if you only manage to claim three Foci). If you find the Antiquity site but don't go into the [[ON:Excavation|Excavation]] mini-game, and instead get a random [[ON:Treasures|Treasure]], you will clear the selected zone from the map and update your Foci count. You may collect a ton of Treasures in this manner if you so desire, by intentionally claiming only a single Foci, but they will always be of {{ESO Quality Color|n|'''Normal'''}} Quality.

You may continue to Scry the same Antiquity until you claim all six Foci, limiting your search to one.

==Difficulty Levels==
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface 00.jpg|thumb|left|{{ESO Quality Color|n|'''Trivial'''}} Scry]]
===Trivial===
There is only one {{ESO Quality Color|n|'''Trivial'''}} level antiquity, which is encountered during the tutorial.  There are three different facet types, and only one Focus to discover.  Since you do not have the more advanced skills yet, you can only use the basic Scry activity.  Depending upon the arrangement of the facets, it may take between 1 and 5 turns to reach the Focus.
{{NewLine}}
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface 01.jpg|thumb|right|{{ESO Quality Color|f|'''Simple'''}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|'''Intermediate'''}} Scry]]
===Simple and Intermediate===
Scrying for {{ESO Quality Color|f|'''Simple'''}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|'''Intermediate'''}} Leads are relatively straightforward. There are five different facet types, and each Foci is symmetrically aligned into two columns, with the closest ones being only four facets away. This means that one can use [[ON:Farsight (skill)|Farsight]] to immediately start off a Scry with a Foci collected. The vertically-aligned Foci also are only a few facets apart; this also means that a use of Farsight can claim two Foci at once, from making a vertical line from the top of the lowest one to the bottom of the highest one.

{{ESO Quality Color|f|'''Simple'''}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|'''Intermediate'''}} Scries can be fully completed by only using [[ON:Scry|Scry]].
{{NewLine}}
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface 02.jpg|thumb|left|{{ESO Quality Color|e|'''Advanced'''}} Scry, showcasing a wider play area and Foci shift]]
===Advanced===
Scrying for {{ESO Quality Color|e|'''Advanced'''}} Leads considerably changes the playing field. Not only are there six facet types now, the Foci shifted into two rows (as opposed to columns), with the closest one being two facets away. Vertically, the outer Foci are six apart, and the central ones three. Whereas the lower difficulty ones can be fully completed without the need to use {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charges, {{ESO Quality Color|e|'''Advanced'''}} Scries will need either decent-enough facet randomness or the use of skills to do so.

Unlike {{ESO Quality Color|f|'''Simple'''}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|'''Intermediate'''}} Scries, [[ON:Farsight (skill)|Farsight]] cannot claim multiple Foci at once unless it has been upgraded. Furthermore, using the ability may be a waste of an initial {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charge unless you approach the closest unclaimed Foci by its side.

[[ON:Coalescence|Coalescence]] may, instead, be the best skill to open up a scry with: not only can it be used anywhere on the grid, it can also set you up with a chain of facets. Once you expand your area of control, [[ON:Dilation|Dilation]] functions remarkably well, as it has a wider reach than Scry while functioning similar to (or, if upgraded, better than) it. As mentioned before, Farsight still has its uses, but is far more useful upgraded unless your area of control is wide enough.
{{NewLine}}
===Master===
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface 03.jpg|thumb|{{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Master'''}} Scry, having a one-hex grid increase and horizontal asymmetry]]
Scrying for {{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Master'''}} Leads is fairly similar in structure to {{ESO Quality Color|e|'''Advanced'''}} Leads. There are now seven different facet types, though, and its horizontal symmetry has broken from the topmost Foci being shifted upwards. The closest Foci is still only two facets apart, but the grid's expansion has shifted the edge Foci to be seven apart, and the central Foci five. This means that [[ON:Farsight (skill)|Farsight]] can only complete two Foci simultaneously if it is both upgraded and used on the two central Foci. It also means that fully completing scries through Scrying alone is impossible without the use of {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charges, and incredibly hard without upgraded skills.

[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface Success 02.jpg|thumb|left|A successful {{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Master'''}} [[ON:Scry|Scry]], with two visible uses of [[ON:Coalescence|Coalescence]]]]
The sheer reach of [[ON:Coalescence|Coalescence]] makes it the best skill to use on these scries, especially if the grid has many groups of facets with the same appearance scattered about. An upgraded [[ON:Dilation|Dilation]] can also use expanded areas of control to the fullest extent, as long as you prioritize horizontal facet movement over vertical. Paired up with an upgraded Coalescence, these two skills can make {{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Master'''}} (and {{ESO Quality Color|a|'''Ultimate'''}}) scries far easier to complete.

Utility-focused passive skills have been largely unmentioned, but for {{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Master'''}} Scries and higher, [[ON:Scrier's Patience|Scrier's Patience]] and [[ON:Future Focus|Future Focus]] can be your saving grace— even at their base levels. The extra turns from Scrier's Patience, and the extra {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charges from Future Focus, allows you to chain facet (and Foci) claims with far more room for error. [[ON:Preemptive Power|Preemptive Power]] can also help a little bit, as it passively boosts your starting [[ON:Scry|Scry]] reach a bit at the start of each round.
{{NewLine}}
===Ultimate===
[[File:ON-activity-Scrying Interface 04.jpg|thumb|{{ESO Quality Color|a|'''Ultimate'''}} Scry]]
Scrying for {{ESO Quality Color|a|'''Ultimate'''}} Leads is the hardest, as it has 8 different facet types. Not only that, the grid has expanded once more, with another horizontal row. The outer Foci are in the corners, at 9 facets apart, and although the central Foci are now only four, they have been shifted to the top. This means that the closest Foci isn't as much of a "free spot" as it used to be, and is now five spaces away from the standard Scry needle.

Like {{ESO Quality Color|l|'''Master'''}} scries, you will have the easiest time fully completing scries if you have at least one or two maxed skills. [[ON:Coalescence|Coalescence]] becomes an integral skill due to the number of facet types there are. In a similar vein, [[ON:Dilation|Dilation]] can help you engulf large swaths of facets, but only if the facet variation around your area control is low.

It is highly advised to max [[ON:Future Focus|Future Focus]], as the extra {{ESO Magicka Link}} Charges will allow for a better setup in your first [[ON:Scry|Scry]] turn.

==Notes==
* Despite the player getting both skill lines at the same time, and the two skills levelling with one another, [[ON:Excavation|Excavation]] and [[ON:Scrying|Scrying]] may not hit max level at the same time.
** In the case of Excavation leveling faster, this may occur when you cause too much damage to the antiquity and are forced to start the excavation over again.
** In the case of Scrying leveling faster, this can happen when you fail to get all the foci in your first attempt, and scry again in order to try and get a better result.
** It's also possible to scry for a lead on one character, and then dig it up on another, which would give Scrying experience to the first and Excavation experience to the second, putting them both out of sync.
* If you update your scry progress by grabbing a dead-end Antiquity spot, then update it again by re-scrying, the dead-end Antiquity site may reappear in the Scry update.
** You can use this knowledge to either grab another Treasure from the same dig site or check the others for the Antiquity spot.
* You can completely bypass the Scry success animation by pressing the Escape key after a. you collect all six Foci; or b. you reach your last turn.
** If you manage to press it too early, it will only have the Scry cancellation window appear.
* You can only have five Antiquities scried at any one time.
* Once you achieve level 10 in the Scrying and Excavation skill line, {{ESO Quality Color|f|Simple}} and {{ESO Quality Color|s|Intermediate}} leads will be the same difficulty as {{ESO Quality Color|e|Advanced}} leads to scry.

Becoming a werewolf adds the related skill line with which you can unlock extra bonuses. {{NewLeft}} __TOC__ ==Benefits and Disadvantages== {{Update|Werewolf Refresh from Update 50 has changed how things work. This section needs to be updated}} Werewolves deal [[ON:Bleed Damage|bleed damage]] with their melee light and heavy attacks which have an increased chance of applying the [[ON:Hemorrhaging|Hemorrhaging]] status effect and have increased stamina and stamina recovery. They can also use their forearms to block and bash, similar to normal weapon use. During the transformation, they retain buffs, passive skills from most skill lines, and benefits of equipped weapons and armor, including weapon enchantments. They also keep active buffs with a duration such as [[ON:Lightning Form|Lightning Form]] after they transform. Unlike in previous Elder Scrolls games, player werewolves can still interact with most objects, change equipped armor and weapons, speak with NPCs (who generally behave normally rather than attacking or fleeing), and end the transformation at will (by using the transformation skill a second time). The main disadvantage of the werewolf transformation is that, while it lasts, the only active skills that can be used are the five from the werewolf skill line. Another significant disadvantage is the limited time on transformations, though this time can be increased by various means using the werewolf skill line. The time remaining of your transformation is shown as a small blue bar under your magicka bar. Also, werewolves will be stunned while transforming and returning to their original form. While in beast form, werewolves are also more vulnerable to [[ON:Poison Damage|Poison Damage]]. Whether in beast form or not, they are vulnerable to extra damage (20% instead of the 10% for humans) from [[ON:Fighters Guild|Fighters Guild]] abilities from players who have the [[ON:Skilled Tracker|Skilled Tracker]] passive skill. You cannot use crafting stations and do fishing while in beast form, you will get a grayed "Your paws are too clumsy" instead of the action text. You cannot use your mounts while in beast form, you will get the message "Your paws are too clumsy to handle reins". You are forced in third person camera while in beast form. All werewolves receive the Lycanthropy bonus, which is active all the time (whether you are in werewolf form or not): {| class="wikitable" !colspan=2|Bonus!!Effect |- |{{ESO Passive Icon|sk|Werewolf-Call of the Pack}}||'''Lycanthropy'''|| You can transform into a savage beast. *Take 15% more damage from Poison Attacks while in werewolf form |} ==Becoming a Werewolf== In order to become a werewolf, you must be infected with the disease [[Lore:Sanies Lupinus|Sanies Lupinus]]. There are a few ways of contracting this disease. One is to be scratched by one of a few special werewolf NPCs. These can appear in [[ON:The Rift|The Rift]], [[ON:Bangkorai|Bangkorai]] or [[ON:Reaper's March|Reaper's March]]. It is not necessary to kill the werewolf; once scratched, you can run away, allowing other players to contract the disease from the same werewolf. A second way you can contract Sanies Lupinus is to be infected by another player who is already a werewolf, and has the [[ON:Shadow of the Bloodmoon|Shadow of the Bloodmoon]] ability. Meet them at one of the [[Online:Werewolf Ritual Site|Werewolf Ritual Site]]s, and the other player will be able to bite you. Each werewolf player can use this ability once a week. You can also approach [[ON:Firralthel|Firralthel]] at one of the [[Online:Shrine of Hircine|Shrines of Hircine]] and ask him to infect you. You can come across him in the wild, be advised by [[ON:Leane Luseph|Leane Luseph]] (who is found in [[ON:Ebonheart|Ebonheart]], [[ON:Skywatch|Skywatch]] or [[ON:Aldcroft|Aldcroft]]) or from using the free Quest Starter from the [[ON:Crown Store|Crown Store]].
